On the SWaT water treatment testbed, Ballast cut the success rate of an adversary's reconnaissance sweep by 85 percent and recorded no safety violation across 50 runs, a 95 percent upper bound of 5.8 percent on the violation rate, against five violations and a tracking error 19 times larger for RL-MTD, the closest published analogue to our design. Measured against the strongest baseline on the physical metrics, a threshold-triggered scheme that itself records one violation rather than RL-MTD's five, Ballast still improves the tracking error by a factor of 2.5 and removes that remaining violation. The gain costs a small and deliberate concession in raw deterrence. Twin inference meets the 50 ms budget on a workstation core and an embedded GPU, and is projected to meet it on both edge CPUs when the three envelope stages are evaluated in a single batched call; the complete decision-to-enforcement path was measured only on the workstation.
Systems and Control.comment: 25 Pages, 14 Tables and 7 Figures

Systems and Control.title: On Over-Conservatism Under Low-Probability Extreme Events: A KL-Regularized Wasserstein Distributionally Robust Planning Method
Systems and Control.summary: The increasing penetration of renewable energy makes power systems more vulnerable to low-probability extreme events, elevating system planning to a critical role in ensuring reliability. Distributionally robust optimization (DRO) based on the Wasserstein distance is widely used to address this challenge. However, we find that the conventional Wasserstein ambiguity set tends to excessively amplify the probabilities of low-probability extreme events, leading to over-conservative investment decisions. To mitigate this over-conservatism, this paper proposes a novel ambiguity set that modifies the Wasserstein distance with a Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence regularization term. By leveraging the KL divergence's sensitivity to relative probability changes, the proposed set effectively curbs the unrealistic magnification of low-probability events. A two-stage distributionally robust planning model built upon this new ambiguity set is developed to optimize the installed capacity of photovoltaic, wind, and energy storage. The complex model is then reformulated as an equivalent exponential cone program with strict theoretical proofs, making it computationally tractable. Numerical results on the PJM 5-bus and IEEE 118-bus systems reveal the over-conservatism of standard Wasserstein DRO under low-probability extreme events and validate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed planning model and solution algorithm.

Systems and Control.title: Fast Analytical Method for Resource Adequacy Assessment in Renewable-Rich Power Systems
Systems and Control.summary: This paper proposes a novel analytical method for resource adequacy assessment in renewable rich power systems. The approach begins by applying the stress strength method to estimate two key resource adequacy indices: loss of load expectation (LOLE) and expected energy not supplied (EENS). This method requires defining the probability distribution functions (PDFs) for both the generation side and the load side. The load is assumed to follow a normal probability distribution, while the generation side probability distribution is derived from the combined PDFs of conventional, wind, and solar power sources. The approach models the cumulative impact of uncertainties on resource adequacy using the central limit theorem (CLT), and improves accuracy with a cumulant based Gram Charlier expansion when the CLT alone is insufficient. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through Monte Carlo simulations conducted on the IEEE single area and multi-area RTS-96 test systems. The results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a substantial reduction in computational time, which is crucial in the context of operational planning, without sacrificing accuracy. Furthermore, its performance improves as renewable penetration increases, making it particularly suitable for future power systems operation and planning.

Systems and Control.title: Data-Driven Surrogate-Model for Real-Time Loads Prediction in Floating Wind Farms
Systems and Control.summary: This work presents a data-driven load-surrogate modelling framework for real-time control of floating offshore wind farms. The proposed methodology uses mid-fidelity simulations performed with OpenFAST and FAST.Farm together with MLife fatigue analysis to generate Damage Equivalent Load (DEL) datasets of floating wind turbines under wake steering conditions. A two-stage surrogate modelling approach is adopted: first, a Feed-Forward Neural Network (FFNN) is trained using data from simulations of a single floating wind turbine, while a second stage corrects the residual error between the FFNN predictions and FAST.Farm simulations using either Gaussian Process Regression (GPR) or an additional FFNN. The results show that the proposed framework can estimate DELs with errors generally below 15% for tower base bending moment, blade root bending moment, yaw bearing moment, and fairlead tension, while maintaining computational times compatible with real-time applications. The study also highlights the challenges related to generalization of the load-surrogate model under varying environmental and control conditions, especially for large floating wind farms. Overall, the proposed methodology demonstrates the potential of surrogate-based DEL estimation for load-aware floating wind farm control applications.

Systems and Control.title: Generic Local Identifiability Does Not Imply Generic Global Identifiability in Linear Networks
Systems and Control.summary: We give a counterexample to the implication from generic local to generic global identifiability for linear networks with a fixed topology, independently unknown edge coefficients, and selected excited and measured nodes. A six-node network with nine unknown coefficients has exactly two compatible parameter vectors generically. Adding six excited and measured nodes preserves this ambiguity while making the added coefficients directly recoverable. The resulting twelve-node structure has forty-two independent unknown coefficients and zero diagonal. For every positive bound on the largest eigenvalue magnitude, a nonempty open set of parameters has two distinct compatible networks satisfying that bound. This holds for both real and complex coefficients. Other open regions have exactly one admissible solution. The proof uses a rational transformation exchanging the two solutions and a common limiting matrix whose fourth power vanishes. Exact rational-number certificates verify an explicit pair. The construction also extends algebraically when the unknown coordinates are whole rational transfer functions. Genericity in prescribed numerator and denominator coefficient families, and the requirement that every transfer function vanish at infinite frequency, remain separate questions.

Systems and Control.title: Estimating Closed-Loop Multiple-Input Single-Output Dynamic Systems using Gaussian Processes
Systems and Control.summary: This paper extends complex Gaussian process regression-based transfer function (TF) estimation from the single-input single-output setting to closed-loop multiple-input single-output (MISO) systems. Accurate estimation of individual TFs in closed-loop MISO systems is challenging as feedback and correlation between measured signals can obscure the contributions of each input. We formulate a Gaussian process-based estimator for MISO systems, provide analytical conditions under which each system module can be separately identified, and show that the estimator converges to the true TFs in the zero noise limit. Moreover, we demonstrate how conventional closed-loop bias handling techniques relying on external excitation can be employed to construct appropriate regressors. Monte Carlo simulations support the analytical identifiability results and highlight the trade-off between closed-loop bias and error introduced by constructing exogenous regressors partly from endogenous signals. The presented work offers an expressive, nonparametric alternative to existing estimation approaches for MISO systems, while providing a probabilistic characterization of the estimation uncertainty.
Systems and Control.comment: Corrected formatting of Appendix C

Systems and Control.title: Amplitude-Dependent Bode Diagrams via Scaled Relative Graphs
Systems and Control.summary: Scaled Relative Graphs (SRGs) provide an intuitive graphical frequency-domain method for the analysis of Nonlinear (NL) systems, generalizing the Nyquist diagram. In this paper, we develop a method for computing $L_2$-gain bounds for Lur'e systems over bounded frequency and amplitude ranges. We do this by restricting the input space of the SRG both in frequency and energy content, and using methods from Sobolev theory. The resulting gain bounds over restricted sets of inputs are less conservative than bounds computed over the entire $L_2$, and yield three-dimensional NL generalization of the Bode diagram, plotting $L_2$-gain as function of both input frequency and energy content. In the zero-energy limit, the Linear Time-Invariant (LTI) Bode diagram is recovered, and at the infinite-energy zero-frequency limit, we recover the $L_2$-gain. The effectiveness of our method is demonstrated on an example that resembles Phase-Locked Loop dynamics.
Systems and Control.comment: Accepted for publication in IEEE Control Systems Letters (L-CSS). This is the author's version, see the copyright notice in the PDF/source file

Systems and Control.title: Preliminary Exploration of Large Models Based on Self-Supervised Learning for Health Monitoring of Power Electronic Converters
Systems and Control.summary: Current artificial intelligence (AI) methods for power electronics converters make limited use of the abundant unlabeled data generated during real-world operation. This underexplored resource holds significant potential for advancing model performance. To address this gap, this paper presents PE-TSFM, a time-series foundation model tailored for power module health monitoring. The model adopts the PatchTST architecture combined with self-supervised learning and is trained on more than 143 million timestamps, where over 98\% of this training data is unlabeled and collected directly from an operating traction converter. In degradation classification tasks, PE-TSFM achieves an accuracy of 87\%, considerably surpassing five conventional time-series AI models whose performance ranges from 27\% to 45\%. These results demonstrate the model's strong few-shot learning capability and generalization across different operating conditions. This work promotes a shift from narrowly focused models in power electronics toward unified, scalable foundation models that can unlock value from large-scale unlabeled operational data.
Systems and Control.comment: Accepted by Proceedings of the 2nd Electrical Artificial Intelligence Conference, EAIC 2025

Systems and Control.title: Network Reconstruction in Consensus Algorithms with Hidden Agents
Systems and Control.summary: Reconstructing the parameters that encode the influence between model variables based on time-series measurements represents an outstanding question in the theory of complex network-coupled systems. Here, we propose a solution to this problem for a class of noisy leader-follower consensus algorithms, where one has access to measurements only from the followers but not from the leaders. Leveraging the directed Laplacian coupling of such systems, we present an autoregressive expansion of the observed dynamics which can be truncated at different orders, depending on the memory of the leaders. When their memory is short, this allows one to correctly reconstruct the full dynamical matrix with hidden leader agents, provided some additional assumption on the system to lift the degeneracy in the reconstruction. We illustrate and check the theory using numerical simulations for the cases of both a single and multiple hidden leaders.
Systems and Control.comment: 4 figures in the main text, 3 figures in the supplemental material, 10 pages

Systems and Control.title: LiDAL-Assisted RLNC-NOMA in OWC Systems
Systems and Control.summary: Optical wireless communication (OWC) is a key enabler for immersive indoor data transmission in future wireless networks. However, managing multi-user interference remains challenging in dense indoor OWC deployments with multiple optical access points (APs) serving multiple users. In this paper, we propose a dual-function OWC system for communication and localization. For data transmission, we design non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) combined with random linear network coding (RLNC): NOMA serves multiple users simultaneously via power-domain multiplexing, while RLNC improves decoding robustness under residual noise and processing impairments. The system is assisted by a light detection and localization (LiDAL) module that estimates users' spatio-temporal presence and location to enable dynamic user association. LiDAL also supports channel state information (CSI) estimation in realistic indoor scenarios where CSI may be noisy and/or highly correlated. We evaluate RLNC-NOMA by analyzing the probability of successful decoding and comparing it with conventional NOMA and orthogonal schemes. In addition, we derive the Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) to evaluate the localization accuracy. The results indicate that RLNC-NOMA increases the probability of successful decoding, and that the proposed unbiased location estimator achieves 44% better CSI accuracy than the baseline CSI estimation and improves the overall system performance.

Systems and Control.title: MagNav: A Dual-Core Magnetic Track Guidance Framework for Lighting-Invariant Navigation in Two-Wheeled Robots
Systems and Control.summary: Two-Wheeled Inverted Pendulum (TWIP) robots are useful for studying how to control systems that are naturally unstable and have fewer actuators than degrees of freedom. Adding autonomous line-following to these robots is challenging because steering and balancing are closely linked. Most existing systems use infrared sensors, which can be affected by changes in lighting, such as sunlight or shadows, making them reliable only indoors. This paper presents a self-balancing robot that can follow a line using a magnetic track guidance system. By using a five-channel analog Hall-effect sensor array, the robot is not affected by optical interference. The control system uses a cascaded PID structure: the inner loop keeps the robot balanced using data from an inertial measurement unit with a complementary filter, while the outer loop adjusts steering based on the magnetic sensor readings. Stepper motors provide precise torque control without needing extra rotary encoders. For comparison, an optical sensor module was also included. Tests show that the magnetic guidance system keeps accurate tracking even in very bright lighting, over 10,000 Lux, while the optical system loses accuracy and sometimes fails. This design provides a reliable, lighting-independent solution for autonomous navigation in places like factories, warehouses, and outdoor paths.
Systems and Control.comment: 6 pages, 10 figures, 1 table. Accepted for presentation at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Signal Processing and Effective Communication Technologies (INSPECT), organized by Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Patna

Systems and Control.title: Control Realization of Schrödinger Bridges over Discrete-Time Nonlinear Systems via Maximum-Entropy Distribution Steering
Systems and Control.summary: This paper shows how a Schrodinger bridge (SB) structure emerges from maximum-entropy (MaxEnt) distribution steering of discrete-time nonlinear systems. We also establish that the resulting bridge can be realized by an optimal control policy. We consider general state and input costs, non-Gaussian endpoint distributions, and input constraints. Assuming the existence of a feasible policy with finite objective value, we show that the state-path measure under a MaxEnt optimal control policy is the unique SB. The reference measure of this SB is induced by an optimal policy of the corresponding terminal-unconstrained problem. Moreover, we give an equivalent characterization of the optimal state-path measure using a killed reference and its normalized Feynman--Kac measure, thereby interpreting the state cost as killing. We then characterize the finite-cost feasibility by the existence of an endpoint coupling having finite Kullback--Leibler divergence from the reference endpoint distribution. For compactly supported marginals with bounded target density, we derive reachability-based sufficient conditions guaranteeing this feasibility. We further provide specializations to fully actuated control-affine and reachable linear systems.
Systems and Control.comment: 16 pages

Systems and Control.title: Enforcing a Strict Safety Margin in LLM Text Generation via Barrier Lyapunov Control
Systems and Control.summary: Large language models are increasingly deployed without formal guarantees against toxic text generation. Existing control barrier function (CBF) based safety filters can keep the generation trajectory within a toxicity-free region, but do not enforce a positive distance from its boundary, allowing formally safe trajectories to approach the toxicity threshold arbitrarily closely and leaving little buffer against modelling errors or disturbances. We address this limitation with a Barrier Lyapunov Function (BLF) safety filter that enforces a prescribed clearance margin throughout generation while retaining the continuous-time transformer dynamics, including feedforward layers. The resulting safe input set is a half-space defined by a constraint affine in the control input, and is non-empty under certified surjectivity and classifier-nondegeneracy conditions. For margin-compatible initial conditions we prove that the clearance margin is never violated and that the prescribed clearance is restored exponentially, yielding an explicit clearance floor, and show that, as the margin vanishes, the admissible trajectories satisfy the exponential second-order CBF condition. We further derive an explicitly computable sufficient disturbance budget under which the clearance guarantee degrades gracefully. Simulations on a small transformer illustrate the resulting improvement in safety clearance.

Systems and Control.title: Safe Unicycle Navigation Among Multiple Obstacles Under Bounded Disturbances: A Learning-Augmented CLF-CBF Approach (Extended Version)
Systems and Control.summary: This paper presents a robust control framework for safe navigation of a unicycle robot to a goal among multiple static obstacles under an unknown, time-varying disturbance. The controller solves a single real-time quadratic program (QP) that combines a goal-reaching term with one safety term per obstacle. The goal-reaching term is a cross-track control Lyapunov function built from body-frame tracking errors rather than a bearing angle, which keeps its Lie derivatives bounded everywhere, including the goal. Safety is encoded using robust control barrier functions, one per obstacle, each tightened by a closed-form, state-dependent disturbance bound. When stabilization and safety conflict, a slack variable relaxes only the convergence requirement, so that the safety constraints remain strictly enforced. Whenever the QP is feasible, the robust barrier constraints guarantee forward invariance of every obstacle's safe set under all admissible disturbances. Complementing this safety guarantee, a Lyapunov analysis yields an explicit ultimate bound on the distance to the goal. A learning-augmented variant replaces the fixed objective with a reinforcement-learning reference, which accelerates convergence when multiple constraints are simultaneously active. We further derive the obstacle separation below which the gap between two obstacles becomes too narrow to pass through under the robust constraints. For such gaps, a learned virtual goal for the Lyapunov function steers the robot around the obstacles without compromising safety. Simulations, a Monte Carlo study, and a comparison against a sampled-data robust baseline support the theoretical results.

Systems and Control.title: Information-based Unified Design Framework for NMR Magnetic Tracking System
Systems and Control.summary: Nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) magnetic tracking offers a promising alternative to magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based localization for medical robotic guidance. However, scalar field measurements and field-aligned marker moments constrain position and orientation tracking, requiring careful configuration design. We present a unified information-based framework that uses local covariance analysis to evaluate receiver geometry, marker separation, and external source configuration in on/off-board NMR tracking. Numerical evaluation shows that planar-array precision depends jointly on receiver count and geometry, with triangular lattice arrays achieving the lowest best-case position uncertainty among the evaluated layouts for 9--20 receivers. Two spatially separated, field-aligned markers enable device-axis tracking, with predicted angular uncertainty below $2^\circ$ at the evaluated workspace center for suitable marker separations. We further establish point-dipole source--receiver duality, unifying the analysis of on/off-board NMR tracking. These
Systems and Control.comment: 6 pages, 6 figures, journal letter submission

Systems and Control.title: Transceiver-Integrated BD-RIS: Wave-Domain Signal Processing for Sustainable and Inclusive 6G
Systems and Control.summary: The shift toward sixth-generation (6G) wireless communications demands transceiver architectures that simultaneously support high-data-rate communications, pervasive sensing, and sub-meter-level localization. Beyond these performance targets, 6G systems are also expected to align with long-term societal goals, including sustainability and inclusiveness. Conventional radio designs, however, remain heavily reliant on digital baseband processing, whose cost, power consumption, and computational complexity scale unfavorably with increasing array size and carrier frequency, making them poorly aligned with these emerging requirements. Beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (BD-RISs) introduce a new paradigm by enabling direct manipulation of electromagnetic waves in the analog domain. This article presents BD-RIS as a wave-domain analog processing unit embedded within the transceiver aperture. By migrating linear signal processing functions from the digital baseband to the wave domain, BD-RISs significantly reduce computational load and energy consumption, enabling scalable and sustainable operation for extra-large antenna array systems. Owing to their ability to jointly provide high operational flexibility, modularity, and energy-efficient analog processing, transceiver-integrated BD-RISs offer a compelling architectural trade-off and emerge as a strong candidate for next-generation wireless transceivers.
Systems and Control.comment: 8 pages, 4 figures, 1 table. Author-accepted manuscript. Accepted for publication in IEEE Wireless Communications, 2026

Systems and Control.title: A Programming, Robotics and Automatic Control Intervention for Secondary Education Students in Sweden and Italy
Systems and Control.summary: This study evaluates the AutoSTEM workshop, an intervention for secondary education that combines a serious game with PID-controlled hardware. Seven workshops were conducted across Sweden and Italy. The six Swedish workshops adopted an explicitly SDT-informed facilitation framework, while the Italian workshop followed the existing educational robotics format without a formally defined SDT facilitation protocol. Self-reports, an objective knowledge quiz, and qualitative responses were analysed using multiple site-adjusted statistical approaches. Technical-specific self-efficacy increased substantially in both conditions, with large effect sizes, while objective knowledge showed only modest, non-significant gains. No significant site-adjusted differences were found between SDT and control conditions for the primary outcomes. Perceived engagement was higher in the control condition, although this finding should be interpreted cautiously. The objective knowledge composite remained positive but non-significant across sensitivity analyses. Female participants reported smaller PID self-efficacy gains than males. Qualitative findings supported evidence of PID learning while identifying technical and pacing barriers. Overall, the results suggest that the technology-rich intervention supports competence development, regardless of SDT-informed facilitation.
Systems and Control.comment: This paper has 40 pages and 10 figures. Partial results have been presented at NPCW26 in Denmark and are available at https://npcw2026.compute.dtu.dk/Yamashita_npcw2026.pdf

Systems and Control.title: Service-Aware Hosting Capacity Assessment of Edge Data Centers with Workload Flexibility
Systems and Control.summary: The growing demand for edge computing, content delivery, and AI services is driving the interconnection of edge data centers (DCs) with distribution networks. Before interconnection, utilities evaluate how much DC capacity can be accommodated without violating feeder current and voltage limits. Fixed peak load representations can overlook service dependent demand patterns, cooling related facility demand, and delay tolerant computing tasks. This paper develops a hosting capacity (HC) assessment model for edge DCs with shiftable workload scheduling. Three representative types are considered: mobile edge computing (MEC), content delivery network (CDN), and AI DCs. Facility demand is modeled by combining fixed base demand, service driven demand, prescribed cooling-overhead coefficient, and a shiftable workload component. Workload execution is optimized under arrival causality, maximum delay, daily energy balance constraints, and the resulting active and reactive loads are embedded in a distribution power flow model. Compared with the baseline without load shifting, the maximum bus level HC gain on the IEEE 33-bus system reaches 4.46% for MEC DCs and 9.89% for AI DCs, while CDN case shows negligible gain under the assumed cache management windows.

Systems and Control.title: Age of Trust (AoT): A Continuous Verification Framework for Wireless Networks
Systems and Control.summary: Zero Trust is a new security vision for 6G networks that emphasises the philosophy of never trust and always verify. However, there is a fundamental trade-off between the wireless transmission efficiency and the trust level, which is reflected by the verification interval and its adaptation strategy. More importantly, the mathematical framework to characterise the trust level of the adaptive verification strategy is still missing. Inspired by this vision, we propose a concept called age of trust (AoT) to capture the characteristics of the trust level degrading over time, with the definition of the time elapsed since the last verification of the target user's trust plus the initial age, which depends on the trust level evaluated at that verification. The higher the trust level, the lower the initial age. To evaluate the trust level in the long term, the average AoT is used. We then investigate how to find a compromise between average AoT and wireless transmission efficiency with limited resources. In particular, we address the bi-objective optimization (BOO) problem between average AoT and throughput over a single link with arbitrary service process, where the identity of the receiver is constantly verified, and we devise a periodic verification scheme and a Q-learning-based scheme for constant process and random process, respectively. We also tackle the BOO problem in a multiple random access scenario, where a trust-enhanced frame-slotted ALOHA is designed. Finally, the numerical results show that our proposals can achieve a fair compromise between trust level and wireless transmission efficiency, and thus have a wide application prospect in various zero-trust architectures.
Systems and Control.comment: This paper has been accepted for publication in IEEE TMC

Systems and Control.title: Constrained Grid-Forming Control for Photovoltaic Systems: A Control Barrier Function Approach
Systems and Control.summary: This paper leverages control barrier functions (CBFs) to systematically account for constraints of voltage source converters (VSCs) and photovoltaic (PV) resources in grid-forming (GFM) control. The proposed control combines (unconstrained) dual-port GFM control with control barrier functions (CBFs) to ensure reliable and safe operation of a GFM PV system under grid faults, sudden changes in irradiance, and load perturbations. First, CBFs are used to encode physical and operational limits of the PV system, namely current and voltage limits at its ac and dc terminals. Then, CBFs are used to restrict the dynamics of dual-port GFM control to within the VSC and PV limits during both transient and steady states. To this end, a cost function is defined that encodes trade-offs between forming the ac voltage phase angle/frequency and voltage magnitude under constraints. Then, real-time optimization is used to make the least modification, as measured by the cost function, to the (unconstrained) dual-port GFM control state to remain within the safe set encoded by the CBFs. Finally, the performance of the developed constrained GFM control is evaluated through EMT simulations in MATLAB/Simulink.

Systems and Control.title: Stability Transfer for Autonomous Systems via Higher-Order Taylor-Truncated Lyapunov Certificates
Systems and Control.summary: We develop analytical sufficient conditions for certifying the local asymptotic stability of nonlinear autonomous systems based on Lyapunov functions derived from their finite-order Taylor polynomial approximations. This approach translates the stability analysis problem from the original nonlinear dynamics to a more computationally tractable polynomial domain. The derived conditions allow for the explicit calculation of a guaranteed inner approximation of the region of attraction ($\mathrm{ROA}$). We show how sum-of-squares (SOS) programming and grid search can be used to systematically search for polynomial Lyapunov functions that yield a large certified threshold radius and extract a certified invariant set inner approximation of the $\mathrm{ROA}$ of the nonpolynomial original system. The framework is then applied to a control tuning problem: finding reduced-effort Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) controllers that ensure that a given initial state of interest belongs to the certified $\mathrm{ROA}$ of the nonpolynomial closed loop system. The effectiveness of the overall methodology is demonstrated using a pendulum with nonlinear damping and a nonlinear control system.

Systems and Control.title: A Collision-Aware Predictive Rerouting Framework for Connected and Automated Vehicles
Systems and Control.summary: In this paper, we investigate the problem of mitigating non-recurrent congestion in urban transportation networks through predictive and adaptive routing for connected and automated vehicles (CAVs). We propose a collision-aware predictive rerouting framework that integrates microscopic SUMO simulation, DCRNN-based spatiotemporal traffic-state forecasting, collision-window lookahead, and multi-objective route scoring. The routing controller uses predicted congestion, live emission information, route-length penalties, and incident-window constraints to decide when CAVs deviate from their current routes. The completed simulation campaign across three urban network scenarios, five CAV penetration levels, three random seeds, and multiple benchmark rerouting strategies shows that the proposed full framework does not dominate all baselines in aggregate travel time, distance, or emissions. Instead, its principal advantage is operational stability: it maintains comparable network-level efficiency while substantially reducing rerouting frequency relative to active rerouting baselines. These results demonstrate both the promise and the tradeoffs of embedding graph-based prediction and collision awareness into real-time CAV rerouting, and they motivate further work on forecast calibration, uncertainty-aware prediction, and system-level fairness between CAV and non-CAV traffic.
Systems and Control.comment: 15 pages

Systems and Control.title: A Decoupled Approach for Modeling N-k Interdiction with Induced Failures in Electric Power Grids
Systems and Control.summary: The electric power grid is a critical infrastructure system subject to different types of failures which can have devastating impacts on society. One framework to study the resilience of the grid is the N-k interdiction model, which introduces an attacker and defender model to identify grid vulnerabilities. However, traditional N-k interdiction models characterize the power grid with steady-state assumptions. One key aspect missing from this analysis is the behavior of the grid as it evolves from the pre-failure grid state and post-failure grid state. During such a transition period, automated protection systems, transient instabilities, and other phenomena can trigger cascading failures that can occur before grid operators can respond. To bridge this gap, this paper first introduces the generalized induced failure N-k (N-k.k') problem, where an initial set of k failures induces an additional set of k' failures. In this context, we propose a disjoint optimization approach that decouples the computation of cascading failures from the interdiction model. This system response model, furthermore, is treated as a black box module without compromising the underlying performance guarantees of the interdiction model. Extensive experiments on several benchmark power grid case studies showcase the efficacy and scalability of the approach.

Systems and Control.title: Full-Order Safety for Nonlinear Reduced-Order MPC
Systems and Control.summary: Reduced-order models (ROMs) make model predictive control (MPC) of high-dimensional nonlinear systems tractable, but the resulting modeling error can lead to constraint violations on the real system. We introduce CoRE-MPC, a robust MPC formulation that plans with a nonlinear ROM and guarantees recursive feasibility and constraint satisfaction for the full-order system. It can be applied with a broad class of nonlinear model reduction techniques and the resulting MPC does not require evaluating the full-order model online, thus ensuring computational efficiency. The key insight is in how the ROM affects the dynamics of the prediction error. We account for this with two error radii that are propagated alongside the ROM and provide a guaranteed bound on the prediction error. The approach is validated in simulation on an 80-state oscillator chain, a Burgers equation, and a 9,768-state finite-element soft robot, where a two-state ROM with data-driven bounds keeps all 1,628 nodes clear of a wall at a median solve time below 1 ms for a 20 ms control period. Across these examples, CoRE-MPC is 13 to 61 times faster than full-order robust MPC at only 27 to 35% higher closed-loop cost, whereas existing certified schemes are either infeasible or at least twice as conservative. Code: [released upon publication].
Systems and Control.comment: 8 pages, 4 figures

Systems and Control.title: Verification and Forward Invariance of Control Barrier Functions for Differential-Algebraic Systems
Systems and Control.summary: Differential-algebraic equations (DAEs) arise in power networks, chemical processes, and multibody systems, where algebraic constraints encode physical conservation laws. The safety of such systems is critical, yet safe control is challenging because algebraic constraints restrict allowable state trajectories. Control barrier functions (CBFs) provide computationally efficient safety filters for ordinary differential equation (ODE) systems. However, existing CBF methods are not directly applicable to DAEs due to potential conflicts between the CBF condition and the constraint manifold. This paper introduces DAE-aware CBFs that incorporate the differential-algebraic structure through projected vector fields. We derive conditions that ensure forward invariance of safe sets while preserving algebraic constraints and extend the framework to higher-index DAEs. A systematic verification framework is developed, establishing necessary and sufficient conditions for geometric correctness and feasibility of DAE-aware CBFs. For polynomial systems, sum-of-squares certificates are provided, while for nonpolynomial and neural network candidates, satisfiability modulo theories are used for falsification. The approach is validated on wind turbine and flexible-link manipulator systems.

Systems and Control.title: Split the Yield, Share the Risk: Pricing, Hedging and Fixed rates in DeFi
Systems and Control.summary: We present the first formal treatment of \emph{yield tokenization}, a mechanism that decomposes yield-bearing assets into principal and yield components to facilitate risk transfer and price discovery in decentralized finance (DeFi). We propose a model that characterizes yield token dynamics using stochastic differential equations. We derive a no-arbitrage pricing framework for yield tokens, enabling their use in hedging future yield volatility and managing interest rate risk in decentralized lending pools. Taking DeFi lending as our focus, we show how both borrowers and lenders can use yield tokens to achieve optimal hedging outcomes and mitigate exposure to adversarial interest rate manipulation. Furthermore, we design automated market makers (AMMs) that incorporate a menu of bonding curves to aggregate liquidity from participants with heterogeneous risk preferences. This leads to an efficient and incentive-compatible mechanism for trading yield tokens and yield futures. Building on these foundations, we propose a modular \textit{fixed-rate} lending protocol that synthesizes on-chain yield token markets and lending pools, enabling robust interest rate discovery and enhancing capital efficiency. Our work provides the theoretical underpinnings for risk management and fixed-income infrastructure in DeFi, offering practical mechanisms for stable and sustainable yield markets.

Systems and Control.title: Kalman-Bucy Filtering with Randomized Sensing: Fundamental Limits and Sensor Network Design for Field Estimation
Systems and Control.summary: Stability analysis of the Kalman filter under randomly lost measurements has been widely studied. We revisit this problem in a general continuous-time framework, where both the measurement matrix and noise covariance evolve as random processes, capturing variability in sensing locations. Within this setting, we derive a closed-form upper bound on the expected estimation covariance for continuous-time Kalman filtering. We then apply this framework to spatiotemporal field estimation, where the field is modeled as a Gaussian process observed by randomly located, noisy sensors. Using clarity, introduced in our earlier work as a rescaled form of the differential entropy of a random variable, we establish a lower bound on the expected spatially averaged clarity and show that its steady-state value converges to a grid-independent limit as the grid is refined. This result exposes fundamental performance limits through a composite sensing parameter that jointly captures the effects of the number of sensors, noise level, and measurement frequency. Simulations show close agreement between the continuous-time analytical solution and the discrete-time covariance, with the agreement improving as the sampling interval decreases. The analytical solution also avoids the recursive computations required in the discrete-time formulation. Most importantly, the derived limits provide principled and efficient guidelines for sensor network design prior to deployment.

Systems and Control.title: Measurements and Analysis of Distortion in Inertial Force Exciters for Flat-Panel Loudspeakers
Systems and Control.summary: Flat-panel loudspeakers are typically driven by dynamic exciters that employ a voice coil coupled to a reaction mass to exert force on the panel. Unlike conventional loudspeakers, where the cone is relatively light weight, heavy panels may require significant exertion from the driver to achieve sound pressure levels required of consumer grade loudspeakers. Overexertion can cause harmonic distortion and reduced sound quality, especially in drivers where the voice coil is not centered in the magnetic field. There are many different exciters available commercially with different power ratings and price points. The frequency response, linearity, total-harmonic distortion (THD), intermodulation distortion (IMD), and force vs. displacement were measured for three types of exciters to determine the consistency of manufacturing and use in panel loudspeakers. These exciters were found to have high variability in all metrics among units of the same type. Distortion metrics such as IMD may be reduced by running impedance sweeps to match exciters with similar response characteristics in multi-actuator panels.
Systems and Control.comment: Accepted to 161st Convention of the Audio Engineering Society, Nashville, TN, USA, Oct. 2026

Systems and Control.title: Learning in Orbit: Onboard Training and Closed-Loop Attitude Control with a Thermal Segmentation Model on a Spacecraft
Systems and Control.summary: Deep space missions increasingly require spacecraft capable of autonomously operating in environments with communication delays and bandwidth limitations. A key enabler of such autonomy is the ability to run learning-based algorithms directly onboard. In this work, we present a flight deployment on a 6U CubeSat that demonstrates (1) onboard training and inference of a thermal segmentation model on an NVIDIA Jetson TX2 NX GPU in space and (2) closed-loop attitude control using the segmentation model on a real-time, thermal image feed to track the Moon. In addition to this demonstration, we implement ROS 2 Foxy as a data transport middleware and integrate an open-source file system that provides strong data integrity guarantees and self-healing features. Over the course of approximately one year, we performed 12 experiments on the spacecraft, advancing the state of the art in autonomous spacecraft systems by showing how modern learning-based pipelines, commercially available hardware, and open-source software can operate reliably under the compute and environmental constraints of Low Earth Orbit (LEO).

Systems and Control.title: Global Parameter Identification and Uncertainty Quantification of reduced-order ADM1 using Maximum Likelihood Estimation and Bayesian Inference
Systems and Control.summary: Anaerobic digestion (AD) models can be challenging to calibrate against real data due to limited practical identifiability, data scarcity, and model complexity. Weighted least squares objective functions and gradient-based solvers using finite differences are often used in literature, but result in suboptimal parameter estimates and large uncertainty bands. This paper identifies the parameters of a reduced-order ADM1 by comparing the frameworks of maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) and Bayesian inference (BI), and quantifies uncertainties of parameters and outputs. Multirate experimental data are taken from a lab-scale AD reactor fed with agricultural substrates and operated at organic loading rates of 3$\,$g VS $\mathrm{m^{-3}d^{-1}}$. Global optima are found via global and gradient-based local search algorithms using forward sensitivities. Enhanced scatter search provides the best global search results. These are refined by the Gauss-Newton algorithm as the best local search, which delivers $R^2$ values of 0.95 for acetic acid and 0.77 for biogas production. BI yields substantially narrower uncertainty bands than MLE and avoids the need for a global search by incorporating prior knowledge about parameter distributions. The search space is captured efficiently by log10 scaling of parameters. Algorithmic details on its implications are provided. Despite a high-resolution lab-scale dataset, the ADM1-specific inhibition parameter $K_\mathrm{I,nh3}$ is practically not identifiable with MLE, and shows a low output sensitivity, whereas a parameter for the effective ion concentration shows superb practical identifiabilty at high confidence with both MLE and BI. The present work lays a scalable base for calibration of nonlinear AD models by providing reliable simulations. It thus advances model-based monitoring and control applications of multirate processes such as agricultural AD plants.
Systems and Control.comment: v1: first upload of extended version

Systems and Control.title: DiffGIPC: Differentiable Mixed-Coordinate Contact Dynamics on GPU
Systems and Control.summary: Contact-rich inverse problems require efficient gradients and reliable enforcement of non-penetration. Existing differentiable methods provide fast simulation and rigid-deformable coupling, but contact treatments based on penalties or velocity-level constraints can permit penetration or positional drift. Incremental Potential Contact (IPC) maintains non-penetration through geometric barriers and {continuous collision detection (CCD)}. However, repeated forward and backward evaluations remain costly in full-space finite-element (FEM) implementations, particularly when nearly rigid components retain many vertex {degrees of freedom (DoFs)}. We present DiffGIPC, a GPU-accelerated differentiable IPC framework for optimizing interacting deformable and nearly rigid bodies. Our affine-body derivatives enable {rest-shape} design, initial-state optimization, and articulated control while retaining only twelve motion DoFs per affine body. These gradients account for how changes in geometry, placement, and actuation affect other objects through collision and friction. We preserve these interactions in one coupled FEM-affine adjoint system per frame, reducing the backward-system size without discarding the dependencies that drive the inverse problem. GPU-optimized backward computation further reduces the cost of repeated gradient evaluations. A reusable PyTorch interface connects supported physical parameters to user-defined parameter maps and losses across design, identification, motion, placement, and articulated control. Experiments demonstrate peak speedups over DiffIPC of approximately 150.0x with full-space FEM and 4133.3x with affine bodies for combined forward simulation and backward differentiation.

Systems and Control.title: Nonlocal Teams and Information Structures
Systems and Control.summary: We look at Bell inequalities from the lens of information structures in stochastic teams. We consider the usual Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) game and a dynamic variant of the same to study how various classes of strategies, classical, projective and quantum, behave under team theoretic solution concepts. We endow players with a fixed quantum state that we take as the Bell state, and allow variation of the measurement strategies. In the static game, projective strategies (where each player performs projective measurements) are team optimal for all parameter values and are closed under best response. In the dynamic game these properties fail: projective strategies may be strictly outperformed by classical ones, best responses to projective strategies need not be projective, and, beyond a sharp threshold on the channel noise, team optimal projective strategies cease to be person-by-person optimal, even though person-by-person optimal projective pairs always exist. These results shed light on the delicate interplay of information structure in quantum strategies and the fragility, under a change of information structure, of structural properties that are taken for granted in the static setting.
Systems and Control.comment: 37 pages, 3 figures

Systems and Control.title: A Performative Control Approach to Day-to-Day Traffic Signal Retiming
Systems and Control.summary: Conventional fixed-time traffic signal optimization and recent day-to-day signal retiming generally model route adaptation under prescribed route-choice behavior and origin-destination (OD) demand, while neglecting the fact that travelers' behavior can be performative to the signal control policy. A signal timing policy learned from historical traffic observations must therefore account for how its own deployment changes the distribution on which it will be evaluated in the future. We formulate this problem as performative signal control under observed traveler responses and characterize performative stability of the coupled policy-demand system. We propose incremental day-to-day retiming using the local policy gradient at the current operating point, estimated offline through simulation-based zeroth-order optimization without an explicit day-to-day demand-response model. This gradual approach provides a feasible path for policy and demand to co-evolve toward stability. Experiments on a downtown Denver network show that our approach improves congestion, throughput, and stability, generalizes across different demand levels, and remains effective when the offline simulator contains mismatched travel demand and routing behaviors.
Systems and Control.comment: 8 pages, 6 figures, 2 tables

Machine Learning.title: Cepheid: Decoupling Scale from Structure for Cross-Family Motion Completion
Machine Learning.summary: Sparse-to-dense motion completion recovers dense mesh motion from sparse vertex displacements. Residual priors trained on one geometry family frequently fail to beat parameter-free harmonic extension off-family. Moreover, cross-family training meets a scaling barrier: residual amplitude varies by more than an order of magnitude across geometry families and collapses as observations become denser. Since this scale depends on unknown target motion, it cannot be measured directly at test time. We decouple residual structure from physical scale by learning a dimensionless prior, estimating amplitude from observables and a lightweight correction fitted only on training sources. Our unified model surpasses harmonic extension across all evaluated families, including unseen cloth and legged bodies, without skeletons, registration, or cross-mesh correspondence. The same prior applies without retraining to point-tracked animal video and a robot grasping a soft body. Project page: https://su-terry.github.io/cepheid-website/

Machine Learning.title: What Matters in Quality-Aware VLA Pretraining: A Benchmark and Empirical Study
Machine Learning.summary: How should demonstration quality be used during vision-language-action (VLA) pretraining to improve performance after target-task fine-tuning? We compare weighting, filtering, and conditioning across reward definitions and label granularities using 5,000 naturally suboptimal human demonstrations and 24 target tasks. Within each VLA, we match demonstrations and training budgets. Additional comparisons examine pretraining data size and the roles of quality tags during fine-tuning and inference. Across three VLAs, we find that approach-aware episode conditioning improves mean success over plain behavioral cloning; conditioning and filtering favor episode and chunk labels, respectively, on average, with model-dependent reversals; and constant-tag fine-tuning improves mean success after conditioned pretraining with either tagged or untagged inference. We introduce AXIS-Bench to support these controlled comparisons. Built on crowdsourced simulation demonstrations, it provides recorded object and contact states for recomputing quality labels on shared trajectories. Replayable trajectories support workspace-aligned rendering and user-defined real-world target tasks. In our real-world experiment, simulation pretraining raises success from 9.6\% to 31.7\%. Project page: https://axis-bench.github.io/.

Machine Learning.title: Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards
Machine Learning.summary: Long-horizon agents have drawn growing attention for their ability to work autonomously -- from hours to days -- on economically valuable tasks, a capability essential to automated discovery and recursive self-improvement (RSI). Yet open-source models still struggle on long-horizon tasks, largely for lack of both training data and a working recipe, and scaling both is hard: long, complex tasks are difficult to curate and verify, and their rewards are sparse. We address both. First, we introduce Tev-Gym, the first long-horizon agent training dataset with verifiable, dense, progressive rewards -- 1,170 verified task environments across 7 domains. It is built on a latent-world-first approach that first constructs a latent world: a complete and correct hidden specification of the task domain, workflow, and expected state after each step. Each task is then progressively rendered from this specification into an agent-facing environment, enabling controllable complexity and a natural progress metric. Second, we turn this metric into a training recipe: via progress-potential reward shaping (PPRS), we convert progress into a dense per-step reward that improves training efficiency and makes otherwise-intractable tasks trainable. Training with this recipe yields Tev-27B, which achieves substantial gains on the Agents' Last Exam computing and math sciences domains (ALE-CM), matching GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5 at Pass@5. Despite training only on ALE-related data, it generalizes to the Terminal-Bench (TB) 3.0 and 4.0 subsets, surpassing GLM 5.2 and Gemini 3.7 Flash, and reaches Claude Opus 4.8-level performance on middle-horizon tasks such as TB 2.1.

Machine Learning.title: Data Free Training of Diffusion Models for Lattice Field Theories
Machine Learning.summary: Sampling equilibrium field configurations remains a major computational bottleneck in lattice field theory, motivating the development of generative samplers that can produce independent configurations. Diffusion models are promising for this purpose, but their standard denoising score matching objective requires samples from the target distribution, seemingly reintroducing the original sampling problem. Here, we show that diffusion models can instead be trained from their own generated samples using the target score identity, provided access to the unnormalized probability density. Importance-weighted formulations of this identity yield a consistent target throughout training, while unweighted variants define a self-consistent fixed-point training scheme. We benchmark the different approaches in two-dimensional \(φ^4\) theory and identify effective choices that enable efficient training and sampling across the symmetric, critical, and broken phases. Ultimately, our data-free training approach achieves comparable performance to training on HMC reference data.

Machine Learning.title: DoubtLess: Training-Free Contrastive Decoding for Efficient Reasoning
Machine Learning.summary: Reasoning models achieve strong performance through long chains of thought (CoT), but often spend more tokens than needed to solve a problem. Existing ways to shorten the CoT require additional training for each model, add a fixed steering vector to the model's hidden states, or use decoding heuristics such as stopping early or banning words like "wait", which can reduce accuracy. We propose DoubtLess, a training-free decoding method in which a much smaller reasoning model steers the large one towards brevity. The small model reads the large model's CoT so far twice, once prompted to be brief (the brief thinker) and once prompted to be verbose (the verbose thinker), and the difference between its two logit vectors, scaled by a strength, is added to the large model's logits at every step of the CoT. On seven benchmarks of competition mathematics, graduate-level science and competitive programming, DoubtLess shortens the CoT of Qwen3-32B by 31% with unchanged accuracy, outperforming five inference-time baselines. We also show that DoubtLess reduces thinking tokens per turn by 20% in a self-debugging coding agent with unchanged task performance. It also generalizes to two other model families with unchanged accuracy. When combined with training-based compression, it further shortens the CoT of a model already trained for brevity. Ablations and behavioral analysis show that DoubtLess reduces repeated checking, with most token savings coming after the correct answer first appears in the CoT. Our code is available at https://github.com/leoluolol/DoubtLess.

Machine Learning.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
Machine Learning.summary: How can we build an agent that thinks beyond human language, yet still acts through it in the external environment? Modern LLM agents still reason and interact through text, while latent reasoning offers an efficient internal medium but lacks native tool access and reasoning transparency. We bridge these two directions with Hybrid Reasoning Agents (HybridAgents), which dynamically navigate between latent reasoning and text-based interaction throughout a unified generation process. Architecturally, a lightweight HybridLink enables seamless transitions between text and latent modes, while the agent's continuous working memory preserves lossless hybrid context across multiple turns. These designs preserve tool-integrated agentic capabilities while making latent thoughts directly inspectable. Building on this architecture, we further develop dedicated post-training algorithms for hybrid reasoning: HybridSFT stabilizes tool-integrated hybrid generation by teaching the backbone to coordinate with HybridLink, then HybridRL scales reasoning by learning when to think in latent space and when to act through text. We evaluate HybridAgent at 3 model scales across 11 benchmarks covering mathematics, science, medicine, search, and agentic reasoning. Compared with frontier LLM Agents and agentic frameworks spanning both text-based and latent methods, HybridAgent consistently improves performance by 10.4%, while delivering 35.5%-54.7% token reduction, 1.8x-2.6x faster inference, and 2.7x-3.7x cost savings. Code and data are available at https://github.com/togethercomputer/HybridAgent.

Machine Learning.title: Exact Topological Compliance: Generating Persistence-Equivalent Graphs
Machine Learning.summary: Persistent homology summarizes the topological evolution of a graph as persistence diagrams (PDs). Generating graphs whose topology matches a target descriptor is increasingly important, yet existing topology-aware generative models rely on soft regularization, producing graphs whose PDs may only be approximately similar. We initiate a principled investigation of the generation problem: produce graphs that realize a target PD exactly. We propose two approaches guided by the implicit local and global constraints a target PD imposes. The local approach builds degree-based PD-equivalent graphs iteratively, and we prove that every output realizes the target PD and that every degree-based PD-equivalent graph is reachable. However, as shown thereafter, local generation necessarily trades off between sample diversity and reaching infeasible states. We therefore recast generation as a global constraint satisfaction problem with a complete encoding solvable by modern constraint programming solvers. This is applicable to any vertex-based permutation equivariant filtration scheme and is minimal under the degree filtration. Experiments on four standard graph generation benchmarks confirm that both methods realize the target PD exactly. Together, our methods provide a principled treatment of strict topology-compliant graph generation. Code is available at https://github.com/Aalto-QuML/ExactCompliance.

Machine Learning.title: Telling FIBS: Probes Effectively Detect Sabotage and Catch Unverbalized Deception
Machine Learning.summary: Recent incidents have highlighted the challenge of monitoring LLM agents and the danger of models deceiving people. We show that white-box deception detection via probes can be scaled up to frontier monitoring settings by collecting the largest deception dataset to date for training probes and introducing a novel probe architecture which can aggregate information across many layers and tokens. Our probes achieve 98.4\% AUROC in SHADE-Arena and 98.0\% in BASH-Arena (vs. 97.9\%, 97.6\% resp. for action-only text monitors) and show improved efficacy as the underlying model is scaled up. We further test probes on several cases where deception cannot be determined from the context alone. In these cases, which we refer to as introspective deception, the ground truth can only be determined through careful elicitation or thorough knowledge of a model's training data. In one such evaluation, we show that probes can distinguish transcripts containing a model's true hidden goal from other goals with an AUROC of up to 99.7\%. Our probes also readily detect deception on prominent open-weight models which lie about politically sensitive topics, and about their beliefs when put under pressure. We release our training dataset, dubbed \fibs, to help drive frontier deployment of effective probes, and encourage the community to expand upon it with further examples of deception and sabotage.
Machine Learning.comment: 11 pages main text, 98 pages total; 18 figures, 18 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/AlignmentResearch/caught-in-the-act-probes

Machine Learning.title: Two Clocks: Why Larger Rollout Batches Learn Slower but Fail on Schedule in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
Machine Learning.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) relies on costly model-generated responses, motivating larger rollout batches and square-root learning-rate scaling. Reported to approximately preserve progress per sample with one optimizer step per rollout, this rule is less understood in practical multi-step training. We develop a two-clock framework that separates the samples needed to make progress from those consumed before collapse. Under a local quadratic model, the square-root rule preserves first-order drift per sample but not progress: larger batches take fewer, longer updates and lose more to curvature, yielding a learning-rate-dependent critical batch beyond which sample efficiency degrades. A drift-threshold hypothesis predicts a complementary failure clock whose sample count remains approximately invariant along the square-root rule. Controlled GRPO experiments on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B across a $16\times$ batch range support both predictions. Ratio clipping delays failure, especially for larger batches, but the progress gap persists without it. Widening the clip trades stability for a transient speed gain. The progress gap reappears on another dataset, a general-purpose checkpoint, and a 7B model. Finally, we use the two-clock framework to derive a simple multi-step RLVR schedule: start below the critical batch and switch to a larger batch before failure. Our code is available at: https://github.com/WinstonLiyt/two-clocks-rlvr.

Machine Learning.title: MFG: Multi-turn Feedback Guided Molecular Optimization
Machine Learning.summary: Multi-objective molecular optimization is a critical process in drug discovery that aims to modify a given molecule to simultaneously improve multiple properties while maintaining a similar overall structure. This process often requires iterative modifications guided by computational or experimental feedback. Recent large language model (LLM)-based methods have begun to explore this iterative approach; however, these methods are not explicitly trained to leverage such feedback, while existing approaches primarily focus on single-turn molecular optimization. To address this gap, we introduce Multi-turn Feedback Guided (MFG) molecular optimization, a reinforcement learning framework that trains an LLM to progressively optimize molecules using feedback from previous turns. MFG introduces a feedback vector capturing both property improvements and source molecule similarity, alongside a feedback-aligned reward function that promotes progressive improvement across turns. We apply MFG over $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O}$, a state-of-the-art LLM model for multi-objective molecular optimization, evaluate $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O-MFG}$ on ten multi-objective molecular optimization tasks. The results demonstrate that $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O-MFG}$ achieves the highest average similarity-constrained success rate ($81.50%$), outperforming the base model $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O}$ ($70.81%$).

Machine Learning.title: Dex4D: Task-Agnostic Point Track Policy for Zero-Shot Dexterous Manipulation
Machine Learning.summary: Learning generalist policies capable of accomplishing a wide range of everyday tasks remains an open challenge in dexterous manipulation. In particular, collecting large-scale manipulation data via real-world teleoperation is expensive and difficult to scale. While learning in simulation provides a feasible alternative, designing multiple task-specific environments and rewards for training is similarly challenging. We propose Dex4D, a framework that instead leverages simulation for learning task-agnostic dexterous skills that can be flexibly recomposed to perform diverse real-world manipulation tasks. Specifically, Dex4D learns a domain-agnostic 3D point track conditioned policy capable of transforming a rigid object from a current pose to a target pose. We train this 'Anypose-to-Anypose' policy in simulation across thousands of objects with diverse pose configurations, covering a broad space of robot-object interactions that can be composed at test time. At deployment, this policy can be zero-shot transferred to real-world tasks without finetuning, simply by prompting it with desired object-centric point tracks extracted from generated videos. During execution, Dex4D uses online point tracking for closed-loop perception and control. Extensive experiments in simulation and on real robots show that our method enables zero-shot deployment for diverse dexterous manipulation tasks and yields consistent improvements over prior baselines. Furthermore, we demonstrate strong generalization to novel objects, scene layouts, backgrounds, and trajectories, highlighting the robustness and scalability of the proposed framework. Project page: https://dex4d.github.io/.

Machine Learning.title: Who Improves the Robot? Toward Physical Recursive Self-Improvement
Machine Learning.summary: Robots are increasingly autonomous in task execution, yet their improvement remains largely human-driven. This study investigates Physical Recursive Self-Improvement (Physical RSI), in which physical experience guides lasting updates to both a robot's capabilities and its improvement procedure, making subsequent improvement more effective across tasks. Physical RSI faces challenges from noisy observations, continuous dynamics, costly trials, and irreversible consequences. We present an L0-L5 framework that differentiates capability-level from meta-level updates and within-task from across-task gains, reserving L5 for independently verified recursive gain. We study existing methods around harness adaptation and model training, alongside safety and control mechanisms that govern execution and successive updates. Our analysis reveals that, despite substantial progress in self-improvement, the surveyed literature does not yet demonstrate Physical RSI as defined by our framework. We identify research priorities in reliable feedback, causal attribution, safety preservation, and benchmarking, outlining a path toward robots that autonomously improve how they learn while ensuring safety. The GitHub repository for Physical RSI is available at https://github.com/SAIL-Research-Lab/Physical-RSI.

Machine Learning.title: Fast Rates for Offline Q-Learning with KL Regularization
Machine Learning.summary: This paper investigates offline Q-learning for finite-horizon Markov decision processes with Kullback-Leibler (KL) regularization. Recent studies have shown that KL regularization can yield fast rates in offline decision-making problems. However, it remains unclear whether Q-learning, which adopts incremental stochastic approximation updates, can achieve such fast rates in the offline setting. We first propose KL-regularized Q-Learning (KLQ), a simple variant of classical Q-learning. By exploiting KL regularization, we prove that KLQ achieves a sample complexity of $\widetilde{O}(1/ε)$ without explicit pessimism. This guarantee, however, has an exponential dependence on the KL regularization parameter and the horizon. To address this limitation, we further propose KL-regularized Pessimistic Q-Learning (KLPQ), which incorporates pessimism into KLQ. We prove that KLPQ retains the same \(\widetilde O(1/ε)\) rate while removing the explicit exponential dependence, thereby further improving the sample complexity. To the best of our knowledge, these results establish the first fast-rate guarantees for offline Q-learning in tabular finite-horizon KL-regularized MDPs.

Machine Learning.title: Scaling Online Optimal Transport Minibatches for Flow Matching
Machine Learning.summary: A central challenge in scaling flow models is maintaining stability in training and integration. In flow matching, this stability depends critically on how source samples are paired with data. Independent random pairing introduces substantial stochasticity, motivating minibatch optimal transport (OT) to construct online source-target couplings that reduce this randomness (Tong et al., 2024). However, as applications extend to larger and higher-dimensional datasets, small minibatches can limit these benefits, while scaling the coupling to substantially larger minibatches at every iteration is computationally prohibitive. Moreover, how OT coupling affects the full stochastic gradient and integration remains theoretically unresolved. In this work, we develop a scalable online entropic OT approximation that enables substantially larger source-target couplings while preserving the benefits of OT. We close the theoretical gap for both unregularized and entropic OT by proving strict reductions in full stochastic-gradient variance and integration error relative to independent pairing, and further characterize how these improvements strengthen as the online coupling minibatch grows. Experiments on single-cell gene interpolation-flow and image-flow training validate these predictions, showing that larger online couplings consistently improve training stability and final generation performance.

Machine Learning.title: RoboSimStudio: An Interactive Toolkit for Rapid Real2Sim of Robot Manipulation Tasks
Machine Learning.summary: It is difficult to accurately model the physics of the interaction between a robot and the objects it manipulates, including contact mechanics, coupled contact dynamics, deformations, stiffness and friction. We present RoboSimStudio (RSS), an interactive toolkit that makes choices of solver, contact model, and physical parameters explicit and editable, allowing both humans and coding agents to iteratively refine simulations based on observed physical behavior. We implement RSS with the open Newton physics simulation system and describe experiments with human-guided real2sim using (1) visual evaluation, (2) force-feedback and (3) agentic Real2Sim2Real. Code, video and additional information can be found on the project website.
Machine Learning.comment: 13 pages, 7 figures, 1 table. Project website: https://robosimstudio.github.io

Machine Learning.title: Localized Operator Learning with Adaptive Partition-of-Unity Mixture-of-Expert Networks
Machine Learning.summary: Operator learning methods such as DeepONets and FNOs often struggle with PDE families featuring sharp interfaces, heterogeneous coefficients, and localized multiscale structures. We introduce a partition-of-unity (POU) mixture-of-experts framework for localized operator learning, in which geometry-aware gating networks produce smooth spatial partitions which blend the contributions of local expert networks. Our main contribution is HiRefPOU, a residual-style hierarchical POU architecture for DeepONets that organizes localized representations through nested parent-child partitions while preserving global continuity. We also show that the same POU principle can be incorporated into Fourier Neural Operators to introduce spatial adaptivity without modifying the underlying spectral layers. On heterogeneous Darcy and reaction-diffusion benchmarks, HiRefPOU achieves substantially lower error than global DeepONet and static POU-MoE baselines, while the broader operator-learning experiments show that the benefits of localization depend on the PDE structure and the chosen neural-operator backbone. The learned partitions are interpretable and align with interfaces and regions of rapid solution variation. These results show that explicit geometric localization can improve both accuracy and interpretability in neural operator learning.

Machine Learning.title: Joint Neural Posterior Estimation and Model Selection for Chemical Reaction Networks
Machine Learning.summary: Simulation-based Bayesian inference for Chemical Reaction Networks (CRNs) must simultaneously solve two computationally demanding problems: discriminating between overlapping reaction pathways and estimating reaction rate constants. Classical approaches, such as Sequential Monte Carlo ABC, rely on handcrafted summary statistics and scale poorly across large parameter spaces. To overcome this, we introduce a neural inference architecture. Our pipeline utilizes shared 1D-CNNs and a permutation-invariant Set Attention mechanism to learn low-dimensional summary statistics from variable-length, multi-experiment time-series data. These statistics simultaneously condition a model selection network to compute posterior model probabilities and model-specific conditional Invertible Neural Networks (cINNs) that estimate parameter posterior distributions. We demonstrate the practical utility of our approach on a real protodeboronation example, illustrating how it handles structural ambiguity and extracts kinetic parameters from competing catalyst deactivation pathways.
Machine Learning.comment: 40 pages total (11 pages main text, 29 pages appendix), 18 figures. Code available at: https://github.com/Esquivel-Arturo/JNPE

Machine Learning.title: Statistical Vignettes on the Grokking Phenomenon
Machine Learning.summary: In this work, we study grokking in a simple, analytically tractable setting whose rich phenomenology allows us to disentangle the effects of initialization, signal strength, weight decay, sample size, and input dimension. These factors can produce superficially similar learning curves through distinct mechanisms, complicating their interpretation. Our analysis distinguishes early fitting through nuisance features, core feature learning, and delayed generalization. We identify sharp conditions under which grokking provably occurs and derive analytic asymptotic expressions for the lengths of the generalization plateaus. Our results also characterize regimes of early generalization and failure to reach a prescribed test accuracy target. We show that the interpolation edge constitutes a distinct dynamical regime, where vanishing spectral gaps separate core learning from generalization, helping clarify the role of proximity to interpolation in existing accounts of grokking. The resulting picture is analogous to fast and slow phases in chemical kinetics and suggests that the lazy-to-rich transition discussed in the literature may reflect a similar separation of dynamical time scales. Our theoretical results are faithfully supported by extensive experiments.

Machine Learning.title: Beyond Single-Model Optimization: Preserving Plasticity in Continual Reinforcement Learning
Machine Learning.summary: Continual reinforcement learning must balance retention with adaptation, yet many methods still rely on \emph{single-model preservation}, committing to one evolving policy as the main reusable solution across tasks. Even when a previously successful policy is retained, it may no longer provide a reliable starting point for rapid adaptation after interference, reflecting a form of \emph{loss of plasticity} that single-policy preservation cannot address. Inspired by quality-diversity methods, we introduce \textsc{TeLAPA} (Transfer-Enabled Latent-Aligned Policy Archives), a continual RL framework that organizes behaviorally diverse policy neighborhoods into per-task archives and maintains a shared latent space so that archived policies remain comparable and reusable under non-stationary drift. This perspective shifts continual RL from retaining isolated solutions to maintaining \emph{skill-aligned neighborhoods} with competent and behaviorally related policies that support future relearning. In our MiniGrid CL setting, \textsc{TeLAPA} learns more tasks successfully, recovers competence faster on revisited tasks after interference, and retains higher performance across a sequence of tasks. Our analyses show that source-optimal policies are often not transfer-optimal, even within a local competent neighborhood, and that effective reuse depends on retaining and selecting among multiple nearby alternatives rather than collapsing them to one representative. Together, these results reframe continual RL around reusable and competent policy neighborhoods, providing a route beyond single-model preservation toward more plastic lifelong agents.

Machine Learning.title: Depth Memory
Machine Learning.summary: Residual connections propagate information through a network by additively accumulating layer outputs. Recently proposed alternatives, such as Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) and Attention Residuals (AttnRes), instead use more expressive depth aggregation mechanisms that improve language modeling performance at scale. In this work, we consider the mixing of representations over depth as a problem of storing and retrieving information across layers. Formalizing this perspective, we introduce Depth Memory (DM), a unified framework that describes the standard pre-layer-norm (PreLN) transformer, mHC, and AttnRes in terms of streams that carry representations through the network. One such stream, for example, could be an explicit memory stream that is queried to enrich the input to every layer, and whose output is subsequently written back into the memory for use by later layers. For AttnRes, this memory stream is a growing cache of explicit layer representations. For mHC, it is an expanded residual stream. Building on this view, we propose Linear Depth Memory (LDM), which formulates information retrieval across depth as a regression problem solved using recursive least squares. The resulting architecture propagates three streams across depth: the standard residual stream, a linear associative memory stream, and an inverse covariance stream. For high-throughput training and inference, we propose a hardware-aware implementation of LDM that reduces peak activation memory and memory traffic.
