We find that PEB strongly depends on how procedural knowledge is represented: presenting the same content visually substantially attenuates exposure-induced shifts in action preference relative to textual presentation. Further analysis shows that this attenuation primarily arises from visual encoding rather than structured layout. Although repeated procedural signals remain recoverable from Visual representations, they exert a weaker influence on downstream action prediction, distinguishing signal accessibility from its use as action evidence. This effect also extends to executable action selection, where increasing exposure more strongly favors the corresponding action under Text than Visual. Layer-wise analyses show that exposure-dependent action evidence becomes more pronounced toward the model output, with stronger evidence under Text, while activation interventions reveal architecture-specific roles of internal components in transmitting or counteracting the preference shift. Complete-agent evaluations across ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, and WebShop further show that Visual skills achieve higher macro-average task success than Text skills for all four evaluated models. These findings establish skill representation as an important factor governing how procedural knowledge is translated into agent decisions. All code is available at https://github.com/NEUIR/Vis-Skill.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: FedSocket: Recipient-Executable Knowledge Exchange for Heterogeneous Multimodal Federated Learning
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Federated knowledge must remain usable by recipients with different modalities, private architectures, and tasks. We present FedSocket, which makes recipient execution a design requirement of the exchanged model. A shared Q combines recipient-computable inputs, task-owned outputs, and ownership-aware aggregation, connecting heterogeneous private models through a common prediction interface. Private models teach local Q copies; the returned Q supports local learning and Joint inference, with only Q parameters and counts exchanged. Across six datasets, FedSocket improves missing-modality recipient accuracy over Local by 14.44 and 15.51 percentage points on MELD and UCF-51. Under matched inference capacity, Joint exceeds independent ensembles by 11.06 points in UCF-51 accuracy and 4.87 points in mean bidirectional Flickr30k R@1. Joint also improves over Q alone on all four heterogeneous endpoints, demonstrating the value of combining local and exchanged predictions. Teacher controls, sharing-path interventions, and component factorials identify the roles of supervision, sharing, and deployment. FedSocket makes exchanged knowledge directly usable from federated training to recipient inference.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Metric Depth Estimation from Arbitrarily Degraded Low-Resolution Depth Prompts
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: We propose AdaDS, an Adaptive Diffusion Sampling framework for prompted metric depth estimation, which estimates high-resolution metric depth from an image and an arbitrarily degraded low-resolution depth prompt. This setting is commonly studied as depth super-resolution, where existing methods typically regress depth directly without an explicit prior over high-quality depth, and thus often produce artifacts under severe or unseen degradations. In contrast, AdaDS exploits the contraction property of Gaussian smoothing: as noise accumulates in the forward diffusion process, the noisy distributions of degraded prompts and their high-quality counterparts converge toward an isotropic Gaussian prior, while the prompt content is gradually erased. Accordingly, AdaDS refines the prompt and estimates its uncertainty to adaptively select a starting timestep, and injects learned noise to place the intermediate sample in a high-density region of the depth distribution learned by a pre-trained diffusion model. Denoising from this sample yields high-quality depth with fine-grained details and corrects residual errors, even under imperfect prompt refinement. Experiments on real-world and synthetic benchmarks demonstrate its superior zero-shot generalization and robustness to diverse degradations.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Omni-Interactive Universal Embedder
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Multimodal representation learning has been shifting from traditional two-tower architectures to large language model (LLM)-based embedders due to their strong instruction-following capabilities. Despite this progress, existing approaches primarily focus on language and image modalities, which also remain the dominant modalities for user-conditioned interactions in current embedders. In this paper, we propose the first Omni-Interactive Universal Embedder (OmniUE), which not only learns a unified embedding space across text, video, and audio by leveraging intermediate-layer representations from dedicated learnable tokens, but also supports omni-interactive querying, enabling users to provide inputs in the form of text, visual regions of interest, and audio spans. Within OmniUE, visual and audio segmenters process diverse user interactions and integrate them with an omni-LLM to produce user-conditioned any-to-any embeddings via context aggregation. To evaluate OmniUE's omni-interactive capabilities, we introduce OmniCHOIR, benchmarking models for omni-interactive compositional audio retrieval based on the given text, video, and audio as well as unimodal or multimodal interaction prompts. OmniUE consistently surpasses state-of-the-art baselines across diverse modalities, with average improvements of 10.4% on textual-interactive video benchmarks (MMEB-v2-video), 1.0% on audio tasks (MAEB), 83.1% on visual-interactive benchmarks (SCaR), and 21.9% on our omni-interactive OmniCHOIR benchmark. We believe that jointly advancing omni-modal representation learning and omni-interactive querying paves the way toward universal embedders. Project page: https://wywywang.github.io/omniue-demo/.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Do Satellites See Commuters? A Critical Benchmark of Vision Foundation Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Satellite foundation models offer a globally available alternative to census data for commuting origin-destination (OD) generation, yet no study has systematically compared encoder paradigms within a single downstream pipeline. We ablate four satellite vision encoders: language-supervised (RemoteCLIP), self-supervised (DINOv3), and geographically grounded (SatCLIP, AlphaEarth) within an identical WeDAN graph diffusion framework across 1,925 US counties, 325 UK districts, and 14 global cities under five random seeds. Three main findings emerge. First, language-supervised features achieve the strongest in-distribution performance (RemoteCLIP CPC 0.602), while geographically grounded encoders transfer more reliably zero-shot: AlphaEarth improves CPC by 33% over RemoteCLIP on UK districts. Second, pretraining corpus scale alone is insufficient: DINOv3, trained on a substantially larger satellite corpus, underperforms RemoteCLIP by 0.091 CPC in-distribution and collapses to CPC 0.022 globally. Third, no encoder transfers usefully to global cities (best CPC 0.122 for RemoteCLIP, 0.022 for DINOv3), confirming cross-continental OD generation remains an open problem. We additionally clarify the semantics of the census noise parameter $η$, whose ordering reverses under cross-continental evaluation, a distinction critical to correctly interpreting prior results. Our code is available at: https://github.com/cruiseresearchgroup/satellites-see-commuters.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: SF-Mamba: Rethinking State Space Model for Vision
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Visual Mamba models have recently emerged as alternatives to Vision Transformers (ViTs), which suffer from quadratic complexity. While the recurrent scanning mechanism of Mamba offers computational efficiency, it inherently limits non-causal interactions between image patches. Prior works have attempted to address this limitation through various multi-scan strategies; however, these approaches suffer from inefficiencies due to suboptimal scan designs and frequent data rearrangement. Moreover, Mamba exhibits relatively slow computational speed under short token lengths, commonly used in visual tasks. In pursuit of a truly efficient vision encoder, we rethink the scan operation for vision and the computational efficiency of Mamba. To this end, we propose SF-Mamba, a novel visual Mamba with two key proposals: auxiliary patch \textbf{swapping} for encoding bidirectional information flow under an unidirectional scan and batch \textbf{folding} with periodic state reset for advanced GPU parallelism. Extensive experiments on image classification, object detection, and instance and semantic segmentation consistently demonstrate that our proposed SF-Mamba significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines while improving throughput across different model sizes. The source code is available at: https://github.com/sony/SF-Mamba.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: From GAN-Based Models to GPT-5: A Taxonomy-Guided Study of Human Performance in Detecting Deepfake Face Images
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Generative models for deepfakes have rapidly evolved from GAN-based architectures to diffusion models and multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, empirical research on human performance in detecting deepfake face images has not kept pace. It remains unclear if (and how) detection performance varies across generative models and whether model-specific training improves detection more effectively than general-purpose training. In this paper, we propose the \emph{Deepfake Face Artifact Taxonomy} (DFAT), a cross-model taxonomy of human-recognizable visual artifacts in deepfake face images, based on which we build both general-purpose and model-specific training materials. Through an online experiment ($n = 524$), we examined human performance in detecting deepfake face images and evaluated training efficacy across five representative generative models: three GAN-based, one diffusion-based, and one MLLM (GPT-5). Our results show that participants' detection accuracy was strongly model-dependent and that images generated by more recent and advanced models were not necessarily harder to detect. After training, participants achieved significant performance gains across most conditions, and their improvement varied by model. Notably, model-specific training generally yielded greater numerical gains than general-purpose training. In a five-month follow-up test ($n = 342$), we observed no significant decline in detection accuracy and no significant increase in perceived stress. Overall, our findings provide actionable insights for designing effective, sustainable, and targeted training programs to counter the growing threat posed by deepfakes.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: AVTime: Reinforcing Dense Audio-Visual Captions with Bidirectional Alignment
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Dense temporal audio-visual captioning is important for multimodal video understanding and generation. However, prior work is constrained by three main limitations: (1) the lack of a dataset combining high temporal resolution, longer videos, and bidirectional alignment between time and events; (2) the reliance of most existing RL methods on checklists; and (3) the lack of a benchmark that bidirectionally evaluates event semantic correctness and temporal accuracy. To address these challenges, we propose: (1) AVTime-50K, a high-quality 50K-scale dataset with temporally precise, semantically accurate captions and longer videos; (2) AVTime, a state-of-the-art model optimized with a novel Bidirectional Temporal-Semantic Alignment (BiTSA) reward that imposes explicit bidirectional constraints between time and events; and (3) AVTime-Bench, a specialized benchmark that introduces a novel bidirectional evaluation of temporal accuracy and semantic correctness. Our code, models, and datasets are available at https://huggingface.co/collections/Apryle/avtime.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Token-Budget Distillation: Transferring Full-Token Semantics to Compressed Video Vision-Language Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Adapting video vision-language models (VLMs) is computationally expensive because video inputs produce a large number of visual tokens, making both fine-tuning and inference costly. Although visual token compression can reduce this overhead, direct adaptation on compressed inputs often causes semantic drift and noticeable performance degradation. We present Token-Budget Distillation (TBD), a parameter-efficient fine-tuning framework for adapting video VLMs under a fixed token budget. TBD freezes the pretrained backbone, updates only LoRA adapters, and integrates FlashVID-based visual token compression into the video pathway. To preserve full-token semantics under compression, TBD employs a dual-path teacher-student design, where a full-token teacher provides stable supervision and a compressed student is optimized with task loss, answer-region KL distillation, GT-anchored margin distillation, and reliability-aware KD control. This design enables the student to recover the semantic behavior of the full-token model while remaining efficient under aggressive token reduction. We evaluate TBD on three video VLM backbones, including LLaVA-Video, LLaVA-OneVision, and Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, across four video understanding benchmarks. TBD consistently outperforms compression-only baselines under both moderate and aggressive compression. On LLaVA-Video at retention ratio R = 10 percent, TBD preserves 97.0 percent of the Vanilla model's average accuracy; on LLaVA-OneVision at R = 10 percent, it achieves an average score of 58.4 and matches 100.0 percent relative accuracy.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: ACM MM 2026. Code is available at https://github.com/Seele77/TBD

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: ContraFM-S2O: Flow Matching-Based One-step SAR-to-Optical Image Translation Model with Contrastive Learning
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: In recent years, diffusion models and GAN-based models have become the mainstream approaches for SAR-to-optical image translation, owing to their advantages, such as high-quality generation and stable training. However, they have shortcomings such as high inference latency and the generated optical images suffer from low detail fidelity, often resulting in blurred edges and loss of fine textures. Thus, we propose ContraFM-S2O, which is a flow matching-based model for SAR-to-optical image translation. Unlike conventional diffusion models, ContraFM-S2O learns to predict the velocity field in training and solves ODE instead of SDE during inference to improve the sampling efficiency. In addition, ContraFM-S2O replaces instantaneous velocity with average velocity along the interpolation path to realize one-step SAR-to-optical image translation and uses contrastive learning to improve the quality of the generated optical images. Experiments show our model achieves state-of-the-art on SAR2Opt and QXS datasets, outperforming baselines, and reduces inference latency via one-step generation.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: After the Federation: Benchmarking Knowledge Portability to Heterogeneous Newcomers
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Once historical clients become unavailable, a federation must serve newcomers through the artifact it leaves behind. How much of its knowledge remains useful in an architecture chosen afterward? We introduce FEDNBO, a seven-dataset benchmark that separates knowledge supply, policy identification, and private-model compilation under disjoint data roles. Controlled studies expose inflated oracle gains, architecture-dependent transfer reversals, and a gap between teacher accuracy and private-model utility. Ordinary public-response distillation provides a competitive reference without public task labels or newcomer samples: gains over strengthened local training are 23.52 and 16.62 percentage points on 300 CelebA identities and 300 FedEMNIST writers, respectively. In a complete-pipeline FedEMNIST comparison, this reference reaches 97.13% accuracy with 12.4 seconds of compilation per architecture, versus 97.03% and 67.5 seconds for a HeteroFedTTA reconstruction at the same epoch budget. Equal-count public-input interventions extend support sensitivity to trainable visual backbones. Together, these results establish an auditable benchmark and a strong reference for evaluating the utility, cost and reliability of post-federation knowledge transfer.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: TamedFlow: Trajectory-Aware Distillation\\for Teacher-Assisted Diffusion Sampling
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) deliver high-fidelity image and video generation, but inference requires many sequential model evaluations. Two acceleration strategies are increasingly important: model compression makes each evaluation cheaper, while adaptive inference avoids selected teacher computation through reuse, forecasting, or speculative execution. Their combination, however, is brittle: directly applying the evaluated adaptive methods to a compressed student can degrade quality, an observed failure mode we call the \textbf{Combination Gap}. We link this gap to a mismatch between pointwise distillation and short-horizon execution: a student trained at teacher states need not remain reliable when its own predictions are chained. We propose \textbf{TamedFlow}, which trains a compressed DiT for this deployed role through cross-architecture feature alignment, a near-identity Velocity Alignment Head, and randomized rollout supervision. At inference, a lightweight Learnable Trajectory Estimator routes completed drafts: accepted drafts bypass the teacher, while rejected drafts roll back and receive one teacher rescue step. Distilling DiT-XL/2 into DiT-B/2, TamedFlow reaches FID $2.58$ at $2.25\times$ measured speedup over DDIM-50 on ImageNet $256\times256$. Ablations support trajectory supervision, and routing controls favor LTE over random decisions at nearly matched latency. Evaluations on ImageNet $512\times512$, MS-COCO, and Latte/FaceForensics extend the empirical scope.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: FrameGRPO: Incentivizing Video Reasoning via Multi-Frame Rollouts and Temporal Credit
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, particularly Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), has improved video reasoning in multimodal large language models. However, standard video GRPO varies only linguistic trajectories while conditioning every rollout in a group on the same sampled frames, which can produce homogeneous rewards and weaken group-relative learning when the shared visual evidence is insufficient or distracting. We propose \textbf{FrameGRPO}, a simple and effective reinforcement-learning framework that requires neither auxiliary networks nor changes to the model architecture. Specifically, FrameGRPO combines two lightweight components: (1) \textbf{Multi-Frame Rollouts}, which use only uniform temporal subsampling of a single maximal-frame decode to construct aligned views that diversify visual evidence and reasoning trajectories; and (2) \textbf{Gated Temporal Efficiency Credit}, which selectively reinforces a correct lower-ratio trajectory when all rollouts in a fixed full-ratio reference subset fail, without imposing an unconditional preference for fewer frames. Extensive experiments across diverse video understanding and reasoning benchmarks demonstrate robust overall improvements over standard GRPO, highlighting temporal-view diversification as an effective mechanism for exploration and credit assignment in video MLLMs.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Curvature as a Baseline: Monocular Pose Measurement of Cylindrical Objects with Dual Colour Stripe Markers
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Thin cylindrical objects offer little space for planar markers. We propose a dual-colour-stripe marker that uses the known curvature of an object to improve pose measurement with a single camera. The boundary between two colours provides a long centre line, while dots and printed edges supply features at different depths. We analyse how this depth separation improves the estimation of rotation about the cylinder axis, or roll. For a camera-facing marker at 15 cm, the Cramér-Rao lower bound on roll standard deviation is 2.00°for a flat marker, 0.38°for a single curved marker and 0.21°for a wrap-around marker. Monte Carlo roll RMS errors are within about 10% of the corresponding standard-deviation bounds. A first-order relation connects the sagitta of the curved marker to the roll sensitivity provided by a stereo baseline. The analytical and simulation results explain how curvature improves monocular measurement and provide a basis for designing marker geometry.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: OncoReg: Medical Image Registration for Oncological Challenges
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: In modern cancer research, the vast volume of medical data generated is often underutilised due to challenges related to patient privacy. The OncoReg Challenge addresses this issue by enabling researchers to develop and validate image registration methods through a two-phase framework that ensures patient privacy while fostering the development of more generalisable AI models. Phase one involves working with a publicly available dataset, while phase two focuses on training models on a private dataset within secure hospital networks. OncoReg builds upon the foundation established by the Learn2Reg Challenge by incorporating the registration of interventional cone-beam computed tomography with standard planning fan-beam CT images in radiotherapy. Accurate image registration is crucial in oncology, particularly for dynamic treatment adjustments in image-guided radiotherapy, where precise alignment is necessary to minimise radiation exposure to healthy tissues while effectively targeting tumours. This work details the methodology and data behind the OncoReg Challenge and provides a comprehensive analysis of the competition entries and results. Findings reveal that feature extraction plays a pivotal role in this registration task. A new method emerging from this challenge demonstrated its versatility, while established approaches continue to perform comparably to newer techniques. Both deep learning and classical approaches still play significant roles in image registration, with the combination of methods, particularly in feature extraction, proving most effective.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Accepted for publication at the Journal of Machine Learning for Biomedical Imaging (MELBA) https://melba-journal.org/2026:029

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: TempoMoE: Identifying and Steering Fast-Slow Thinking Experts for Efficient Multimodal Reasoning
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Multimodal Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) reasoning models rely on long chain-of-thought (CoT) for complex tasks, yet often overthink easy inputs, increasing token cost and latency, and sometimes degrading accuracy. Existing methods optimize reasoning length during training or impose external control at inference, but leave the underlying reasoning mechanism a black box. We find that fast and slow thinking exhibit distinct expert-routing patterns: holding the input fixed and varying only the prompted reasoning tempo produces stable routing shifts. Suppressing slow-thinking experts shortens the reasoning chain, whereas suppressing fast-thinking experts lengthens it, providing causal evidence that these experts influence reasoning depth. Based on this finding, we propose TempoMoE, a training-free, two-stage framework. It identifies fast- and slow-thinking experts via tempo-contrastive routing analysis and redistributes routing weights within the original top-k set according to sample difficulty. It amplifies fast-thinking experts and suppresses slow-thinking experts on easy inputs and reverses this adjustment on hard ones, enabling difficulty-adaptive control over reasoning depth. We evaluate TempoMoE on Kimi-VL, Qwen3-VL, and ERNIE-4.5-VL across six benchmarks. Compared with Vanilla, TempoMoE consistently improves accuracy while reducing output tokens, with accuracy gains of up to 2.6 points and token reductions of up to 35.4%.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Not Another Text Benchmark: Putting the "Visual" Back in Visual Question Answering for Large Video Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Large video models have exhibited impressive performance on a wide range of visual question answering tasks, owing to the rise of powerful, pretrained text and vision encoders. The usefulness of such models have also been demonstrated on a wide range of benchmarks, with an important caveat - the dominant approach in these benchmarks evaluates multiple choice reasoning via text options. This is a natural way to test text-based reasoning in these models, and has led to significant insights regarding model behavior in the community. In this work, we ask a different question - what happens when the evaluation modality is visual, rather than text? We introduce three new vision-centric evaluation benchmarks in temporal frame retrieval, video future prediction, and causal memory distortion, all designed around evaluating visual understanding capabilities in large video models. Our approach complements the existing approaches to evaluate video understanding in frontier models. We show that current frontier models exhibit significant weakness when attempting to reason through visual queries, rather than text. We conclude with an extended analysis section that provides pointers for future improvements in visual understanding for large video models.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: LLM as a Tool, Not an Agent: Code-Mined Tree Transformations for Neural Architecture Search
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Neural Architecture Search (NAS) aims to automatically discover high-performing deep neural network (DNN) architectures. However, conventional algorithm-driven NAS relies on carefully hand-crafted search spaces to ensure executability, which restricts open-ended exploration. Recent coding-based agentic approaches using large language models (LLMs) reduce manual design, but current LLMs struggle to reliably generate complex, valid architectures, and their proposals are often biased toward a narrow set of patterns observed in their training data. To bridge reliable algorithmic search with powerful LLM assistance, we propose LLMasTool, a hierarchical tree-based NAS framework for stable and open-ended model evolution. Our method automatically extracts reusable modules from arbitrary source code and represents full architectures as hierarchical trees, enabling evolution through reliable tree transformations rather than code generation. At each evolution step, coarse-level planning is governed by a diversity-guided algorithm that leverages Bayesian modeling to improve exploration efficiency, while the LLM resolves the remaining degrees of freedom to ensure a meaningful evolutionary trajectory and an executable generated architecture. With this formulation, instead of fully agentic LLM approaches, our method explores diverse directions beyond the inherent biases in the LLM. Our method improves over existing NAS methods by 0.69, 1.83, and 2.68 points on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet16-120, demonstrating its effectiveness.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: On the Benefits of Uncertainty Estimation for Species Classification: A Case Study on Optimizing Expert re-Annotation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Automated identification of diatoms from microscopic images is a cornerstone of large-scale freshwater biomonitoring, yet the high diversity of species and strong class imbalance pose significant challenges for reliable classification. In this study, we develop a ResNet-18 baseline for a 759-class diatom dataset and investigate how calibrated confidence estimates support selective classification to reduce expert workload without sacrificing taxonomic integrity. While the initial model exhibits overconfidence with an Expected Calibration Error (ECE) of 0.117, post-hoc temperature scaling (T = 2.12) dramatically improves reliability, lowering the ECE to 0.055.By leveraging these calibrated probabilities within a triage framework, we demonstrate that a Selective Macro-F1 score of 99.01% can be maintained at 66.2% coverage (rejection threshold $τ$ = 0.934). Qualitative analysis reveals that the system effectively functions as an intelligent filter, consistently deferring rare taxa-such as AAMB and AASI-and ambiguous morphologies for expert review. Our findings, supported by the torch-uncertainty framework, highlight the potential of simple calibration techniques to make automated diatom identification practical and robust, prioritizing the preservation of rare species metrics essential for ecological assessment. To support reproducibility, our code, environment specifications, and calibration results are available anonymously at https://anonymous.4open. science/r/greenprwksp-B53D/README.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Token-Set Choice Confounds POPE: A Systematic Audit of Yes/No Extraction in VLM Hallucination Evaluation
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: We set out to reproduce a recent hallucination-mitigation result on the POPE benchmark. The LLaVA-1.5-7B baseline we measured, 82.21 F1 on the adversarial split, sat 1.21 to 8.67 points above the adversarial baselines we planned to compare against (81.00, 79.30, and 73.54). We looked at the evaluation code and found a readout choice that moves F1 on its own. A two-token logit readout decides yes versus no by comparing two vocabulary IDs, 3582 ("yes") and 1217 ("no"). Across 9,000 greedy-decode questions spanning all three splits, neither ID is generated even once. The model emits " Yes" (token 3869) and " No" (token 1939), because SentencePiece prepends a space byte after the prompt suffix "ASSISTANT:". Read with an eight-token lookup that covers the space-prefixed surface forms, LLaVA-1.5-7B scores F1 0.8221, 0.8498, and 0.8713 on the adversarial, popular, and random splits. That 6.13-point adversarial shift exceeds the adversarial gain reported by five of the six papers we surveyed. None of them states its readout, and our reference ran under 4-bit NF4 quantization, so we cannot say how much of any reported gain a matched evaluation would keep. That comparison stays unresolved until readout and precision are matched. On the fixed baseline we run nine inference-time corrections of our own (none beat it) and dissect why the adversarial split resists logit-level intervention. In a 3,000-question probe, wrong predictions draw more image attention than correct ones (Cohen's $d=-0.46$, $p=1.4\times10^{-24}$), the opposite of what grounding-based corrections assume. A four-readout audit across four further VLMs from three tokenizer families confirms the confound is protocol-level, not model-specific: porting the LLaVA-1.5 IDs verbatim drops F1 to 0.00 on the two disjoint-vocabulary models, whereas a tokenizer-derived readout holds between 0.80 and 0.92.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Accepted at the VLM4RWD workshop, NeurIPS 2026 (poster). 21 pages, 10 figures. Code: https://github.com/Kesav2k04/ugaa-research

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Distill the Visual Evidence, Not Just the Answer: Cross-World On-Policy Distillation for Vision-Language Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: A central goal of vision-language model (VLM) distillation is to transfer both the teacher's language capabilities and its visual understanding. However, existing methods primarily supervise the student's output, leaving visual understanding implicit. Our analysis reveals that a student can match the teacher's answer without relying on the same visual evidence, raising the question: how can we ensure the student responds to the visual information that actually determines the answer? To this end, we propose \textbf{Cross-World On-Policy Distillation (CW-OPD)}, which explicitly supervises the student's response to changes in visual evidence. For each example, CW-OPD constructs two visual worlds that share the question and scene context but differ in answer-critical evidence, yielding different answers. We perform on-policy distillation in both worlds and distill the teacher's cross-world belief transition, encouraging the student to match not only \emph{what} the teacher predicts but also \emph{why} its prediction changes with the evidence. A gradient analysis shows that this term is invariant to errors shared by both worlds and supplies a corrective signal invisible to endpoint matching alone. In this way, CW-OPD makes reliance on the relevant visual evidence an explicit distillation target rather than an implicit consequence of output matching. To diagnose whether a model truly grounds its answers in visual evidence, we introduce CWBench, which measures cross-world consistency via Cross-World Pair Accuracy (CWPA). Experiments on Qwen3.5-4B show that CW-OPD outperforms the strongest baseline by \textbf{1.2} points on average, and the 4B student exceeds DeepSeek-V4.1 (552B) by \textbf{22.4} CWPA points on CWBench. Code is released in https://github.com/baokou-fw2/CWAD.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: This withdrawal is requested because the current preprint was submitted in error using an incorrect journal template, resulting in significant formatting inconsistencies. The authors intend to correct the template and resubmit a properly formatted version. We apologize for any inconvenience.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: HORIA: 4D Human and Object Reconstruction from a Monocular Video with Interaction-Aware Re-Rendering
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Joint 4D reconstruction of a human and object from a monocular video is essential for understanding how people interact with their environment. While recent methods have made noticeable progress, capturing such human-object interactions remains difficult due to two main challenges. First, a video typically contains composite semantic context spanning multiple interaction phases, making it difficult to track the temporal changes of the interaction in the reconstruction. Second, under human-object occlusion, a single-view observation contains incomplete visual information about the interaction, resulting in geometrically inconsistent reconstructions. To address these challenges, we introduce HORIA, built upon two core designs. First, we decompose the entire input video into temporally grounded and semantically distinct interaction phases with motion-aware captioning, obtaining a specific text description for each phase. Second, conditioned on these text descriptions of the interaction, we propose an interaction-aware re-rendering that compensates for the limited single-view observation. Specifically, we render the initially reconstructed 4D human and object from novel viewpoints and refine the renderings with a text-to-video diffusion prior, which provides auxiliary novel-view supervision beyond single-view cues. As a result, our framework produces temporally coherent and accurate 4D reconstructions under diverse interaction scenarios, achieving state-of-the-art performance.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: OmniGround: Strengthening Omni-Modal Temporal Grounding via Attention-Consistency Training
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Omni-modal large language models can jointly understand video, audio, and text, yet they remain weak at temporal grounding, a capability essential for real-world audio-visual applications. To understand this limitation, we look beyond final predictions and examine the model's internal temporal evidence. We identify a temporal generation gap: the internal attention of the model localizes the target moment more accurately than the timestamps it generates. To close this gap, we propose TACG (Temporal Attention-Consistency Grounding), a post-training method that treats internal attention as a reliable temporal pivot and aligns it with both the model prediction and the ground-truth annotation through attention-consistency training. We further build a 580K-sample training dataset by reconstructing temporal QA from dense audio-visual annotations and organizing general omni-modal instruction data. Using TACG and this training dataset, we train OmniGround, a general-purpose omni-modal model with stronger temporal grounding capability, without injecting any additional temporal cues. OmniGround reaches state-of-the-art omni-modal temporal grounding, including 37.5 mIoU on LongVALE and 35.7 mIoU on UnAV-100, while staying competitive on both general audio-visual understanding and vision-only grounding.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: CondenseVLA: Learnable History Condensation for Efficient Multi-Frame VLA
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Robot manipulation often depends on short-term cues - such as brief contacts, temporary occlusions, and intermediate object states - that are ambiguous in a single frame and can only be resolved by integrating observations over time. However, injecting historical information solely by enlarging the history window is computationally costly and frequently yields limited gains due to substantial redundancy and task-agnostic, inflexible sampling of observations. We propose CondenseVLA, a multi-frame VLA policy with a learnable decoder-side history condensation module for using short-term visual context in action decoding. Given a sequence of cached per-frame features from the VLM backbone, CondenseVLA distills observation history into a fixed set of slot tokens using learnable queries and multi-head cross-attention. Simple auxiliary regularization penalizes overlap among slot attention maps and decorrelates slot embeddings, encouraging complementary attention and reducing slot redundancy. Across the evaluated tasks, CondenseVLA improves Simpler-WidowX success from 58.7% to 69.8% (+11.1 percentage points), achieves 97.2% on LIBERO, and reaches 52.8% on real-world tasks. It achieves 21.6% success on memory-dependent RMBench tasks. These results support selective condensation of bounded recent visual evidence for action decoding, while harder multi-observation tasks expose the limits of a finite history window. Project page: https://github.com/FeiyangHong/CondenseVLA
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 39 pages, including supplementary material and the NeurIPS paper checklist. Project page: https://github.com/FeiyangHong/CondenseVLA

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: MIRA: A Multimodal Illustrated Deep Research Agent for Controllable Reports
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Deep research agents are increasingly capable of searching the open web and synthesizing evidence, yet they remain poorly suited to controllable report generation in multimodal deep research. This task requires agents to handle interleaved textual and visual inputs, gather multimodal evidence through multi-step web search, and deliver comprehensive illustrated reports under user-specified requirements. Existing systems face two limitations. During reasoning, they often underuse images discovered along the search trajectory; during generation, they tend to produce fixed-form answers with limited control over report granularity, multimodal composition, and evidence grounding. We introduce MIRA, a Multimodal Illustrated Deep Research Agent for controllable reports. MIRA integrates textual and visual evidence throughout research and writing. At its core, MIRA-Harness translates user requirements into generation contracts and connects four stages: evidence collection, report submission, feedback-driven revision, and final delivery. Building on this harness, MIRA-Data constructs high-quality multi-hop multimodal research trajectories, and we post-train foundation models to operate within the workflow. Using Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, MIRA achieves state-of-the-art performance among open agents on 7 representative, established multimodal-search and deep-research-agent benchmarks, while producing user-aligned illustrated reports with traceable textual and visual evidence.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: SAPO: Self-Supervised Attention Policy Optimization for Improving Temporal Video Grounding in Vision-Language Models
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Video vision-language models (VLMs) have strong semantic understanding, yet remain unreliable at precise temporal grounding. Existing gains from explicitly aligning video frames with absolute time suggest that VLMs may already encode accurate temporal locations internally but lose precision when expressing them as timestamps. Our analysis across four VLMs and two grounding datasets confirms this hypothesis: attention intervals outperform predicted intervals on approximately 66% of valid examples. We term this discrepancy the temporal generation gap. Because precise temporal annotations are expensive, this finding motivates closing the gap to improve temporal grounding using only unlabeled video-query pairs. We propose Self-Supervised Attention Policy Optimization (SAPO), which uses internal temporal attention as self-supervision for Group Relative Policy Optimization and applies a ground-truth-free criterion to select high-value samples. SAPO consistently improves temporal grounding across multiple datasets and models spanning weak to strong initial grounding ability. Relative mIoU gains reach 33.7% on Qwen2.5-VL-3B and 5.4% on the strong Time-R1-7B. The improvements transfer across datasets while preserving general video understanding.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: LEAP: Accelerating ODE-based Diffusion Sampling with Optimal Linear Leaps
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Diffusion models primarily rely on general-purpose ODE-based numerical methods for training-free accelerated sampling, but performance degrades with coarse time discretization. In this paper, we propose optimal linear leaps (LEAP), a specialized method grounded in theoretical and empirical investigations of sampling trajectory geometry. Built upon low-dimensionality and cross-trajectory consistency, LEAP formulates a supervised least-squares optimization problem within the local trajectory subspace, achieving a precise approximation of future states without model evaluations. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LEAP outperforms previous methods across diverse modalities, including text-to-image (Stable Diffusion 3.5, FLUX.1-dev) and image-to-3D (TRELLIS.2) generation. Furthermore, LEAP can be seamlessly integrated into existing solver-based methods, offering a plug-and-play enhancement for modern diffusion models. Code is available at https://github.com/zju-pi/LEAP.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Fundus-R1: Training a Fundus-Reading MLLM on Public Data
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Fundus imaging such as CFP, OCT and UWF is crucial for the early detection of retinal anomalies and diseases. Fundus image understanding, due to its knowledge-intensive nature, poses a challenging vision-language task. An emerging approach to addressing the task is to post-train a generic multimodal large language model (MLLM), either by supervised finetuning (SFT) or by reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), on a considerable amount of in-house samples paired with high-quality clinical reports. However, these valuable samples are not publicly accessible, which not only hinders reproducibility but also practically limits research to few players. To overcome the barrier, we make a novel attempt to train a reasoning-enhanced fundus-reading MLLM, which we term Fundus-R1, using exclusively public datasets, wherein over 94\% of the data are annotated with only image-level labels. Our technical contributions are two-fold. First, we propose a RAG-based method for composing image-specific, knowledge-aware reasoning traces. Such auto-generated traces link visual findings identified by a generic MLLM to the image labels in terms of ophthalmic knowledge. Second, we enhance RLVR with a process reward that encourages self-consistency of the generated reasoning trace in each rollout. Extensive experiments on three fundus-reading benchmarks, i.e., FunBench, Omni-Fundus and GMAI-Fundus, show that Fundus-R1 clearly outperforms multiple baselines, including its generic counterpart (Qwen2.5-VL) and a stronger edition post-trained without using the generated traces. This work paves the way for training powerful fundus-reading MLLMs with publicly available data.

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Multi-scale Fusion of Fast Vision Mamba and Foundation Model Features for Patch-Level Gleason Grading in Computational Pathology
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Automated Gleason grading of prostate whole slide images (WSIs) enables faster and more consistent cancer risk stratification. However, it remains a challenging task due to the subtle morphological differences between grades, the severe class imbalance arising from rare patterns, and the diagnostic features that span multiple spatial scales. Pathology foundation models (FMs) extract strong patch representations but often operate at a single-scale, which limits spatial context and disproportionately affects classes that depend on broader context. The challenge of fusing multiple scales and complementary models, with minimal data and computational resources, remains unresolved. We propose a multi-scale classifier built on state-space models. Our method combines two complementary feature sources: a frozen foundation model, and a lightweight FastVim, pre-trained on ImageNet and distilled from the foundation model, that reads the raw image crops. At each scale, a Mamba model encodes the features from both sources with linear-time spatial context, and a jointly trained head fuses the encoded representations into one prediction. On the PANDA dataset, our method reaches macro F1 of 0.894 and Gleason 5 F1 of 0.802 under 5-fold cross-validation, a 12% and 21% relative improvement over the best single-scale model. A controlled study over 5 foundation models, 5 base classifiers and 3 scales confirms that the gain holds across encoders, with larger improvements observed at smaller scales.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: 13 pages, 4 figures and 4 tables (including supplementary), Accepted to COMPAYL workshop MICCAI 2026, Comments are welcome!

Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.title: Out-of-Distribution Detection in Continual Learning
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.summary: Out-of-distribution detection in continual learning (OOD-CL) is highly challenging, as it requires (i) learning a sequence of tasks without catastrophic forgetting, and (ii) identifying unknown samples (OOD) without access to known (in-distribution (ID)) data from past tasks, where standard confidence-based OOD scores tend to degrade. Existing methods largely rely on a rehearsal buffer of past data or assume closed-world settings, limiting their scalability and reliability in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we propose a novel OOD detection framework for rehearsal-free continual learning, inspired by Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN), which mitigate catastrophic forgetting via their inherent local neuroplasticity. To better leverage KAN in OOD-CL, we introduce a task-adaptive classifier architecture, TA-KAN, which mitigates recency bias and enhances ID--OOD separability through task-specific control of activation locality. Furthermore, we propose a geometry-guided OOD score that complements TA-KAN classifier confidence without relying on past ID data. Our method significantly improves OOD detection while maintaining strong ID classification performance, achieving state-of-the-art results in OOD-CL.
Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition.comment: Accepted at the 40th Annual Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)

Signal Processing.title: Doppler-compensated Space-time Coding for MIMO PMCW Radar
Signal Processing.summary: Phase modulated continuous wave (PMCW) radar is an attractive choice for automotive sensing due to its high dynamic range, interference robustness, and support for integrated communication and sensing. In multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) PMCW radar, code division multiplexing (CDM) separates transmit signals, but non-ideal auto- and cross-correlation properties increase range sidelobes and degrade dynamic range. This paper proposes a Doppler-compensated space-time coding (STC)-based MIMO PMCW radar framework that separates transmit signals before range correlation, eliminating cross-correlation terms under perfect compensation and allowing the same binary sequence to be used across transmit antennas. The Doppler influence on STC decoding is analytically characterized, showing that chip-wise and inter-STC-slot phase distortions increase range sidelobes and generate ghost components in the direction-of-arrival (DOA) spectrum. To mitigate these effects, Doppler is estimated first, followed by joint fast-time and STC-slot compensation before decoding. Residual STC leakage under imperfect Doppler estimation is quantified, and the processing is extended to multiple moving targets through Doppler-bin-dependent compensation. Theoretical analysis and simulation results demonstrate reduced range sidelobes and suppression of DOA ghosts, while maintaining flexibility in code sequence design.
Signal Processing.comment: Under review for a publication in IEEE Transactions on Signal Processing

Signal Processing.title: Leveraging Movable-Element STARS for RSMA-SWIPT Under Practical System Imperfections
Signal Processing.summary: We study a robust multiuser framework for simultaneous wireless information and power transfer (SWIPT), where rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) is integrated with a movable-element simultaneously transmitting and reflecting surface (ME-STARS). By allowing the STARS elements to change their positions in addition to controlling the reflection and transmission coefficients, the proposed architecture provides additional spatial flexibility for improving the cascaded channels toward users in both regions. Meanwhile, RSMA is employed to manage multiuser interference, while power-splitting receivers enable simultaneous information decoding and energy harvesting. The system design further accounts for channel state information (CSI) uncertainty, residual transceiver hardware impairments (HIs), and the nonlinear characteristics of practical energy-harvesting circuits. Accordingly, a robust sum-rate maximization problem is formulated by jointly designing the BS precoders, common-rate allocation, ME-STARS reflection/transmission coefficients, power-splitting (PS) ratios, and movable-element positions. The resulting formulation is highly non-convex because the movable-element positions affect the cascaded channels non-linearly and are tightly coupled with the remaining design variables. To obtain a tractable solution, the joint design is decomposed into active beamforming, passive beamforming, movable-element positioning, and PS-ratio optimization blocks, which are updated iteratively through suitable convex reformulations. Numerical results show that the proposed framework delivers higher sum rates than the considered benchmark schemes, exhibits robust behavior under CSI uncertainty and residual HIs, and achieves stable convergence across the considered system configurations.
Signal Processing.comment: 14 pages, 9 figures

Signal Processing.title: Sensitivity and Identifiability of Tumor-Related Changes in Longitudinal Microwave Breast Imaging
Signal Processing.summary: Microwave imaging could monitor breast tumor response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy, but between-visit changes in breast positioning and normal tissue may confound tumor-related changes. We use eight patient-specific dielectric models from longitudinal MRI of two patients at four time points. For each model, 24-port S-parameters were simulated from 1 to 3 GHz, and Jacobians computed for tumor permittivity and loss, fibroglandular tissue (FGT) permittivity, and breast rotation and translation. 1 mm positioning changes produced changes 20 to 50 times larger than a 10% tumor permittivity change above 2 GHz. Nevertheless, tumor sensitivity patterns were weakly aligned with positioning patterns, tumor-FGT similarity exceeded 0.8 at only some visits, and the Jacobians remained well conditioned. Tumor responses are thus small but separable; monitoring will require positioning correction, frequency selection, and noise-aware detectability analysis.

Signal Processing.title: TapID: Rapid touch interaction in virtual reality using wearable sensing
Signal Processing.summary: Current Virtual Reality systems typically use cameras to capture user input from controllers or free-hand mid-air interaction. In this paper, we argue that this is a key impediment to productivity scenarios in VR, which require continued interaction over prolonged periods of time---a requirement that controller or free-hand input in mid-air does not satisfy. To address this challenge, we bring rapid touch interaction on surfaces to Virtual Reality---the input modality that users have grown used to on phones and tablets for continued use. We present TapID, a wrist-based inertial sensing system that complements headset-tracked hand poses to trigger input in VR. TapID embeds a pair of inertial sensors in a flexible strap, one at either side of the wrist; from the combination of registered signals, TapID reliably detects surface touch events and, more importantly, identifies the finger used for touch. We evaluated TapID in a series of userstudies on event-detection accuracy (F1 = 0.997) and hand-agnostic finger-identification accuracy (within-user: F1 = 0.93; across users: F1 = 0.91 after 10 refinement taps and F1 = 0.87 without refinement) in a seated table scenario. We conclude with a series of applications that complement hand tracking with touch input and that are uniquely enabled by TapID, including UI control, rapid keyboard typing and piano playing, as well as surface gestures.
Signal Processing.comment: accepted to IEEE VR 2021

Signal Processing.title: Bombadil: A Foundation Model for Plant Electrophysiology
Signal Processing.summary:
Living plants, like animals, use electrical signals to carry information about their physiological state across their body, from roots to branches. These signals can be recorded, as they are in animals, from a pair of differential extracellular electrodes inserted into signal-conducting tissue. While machine-learning models have been trained to predict specific plant stress states from these signals, each of these models has been trained for only a single task and none have been designed to transfer across tasks, species, or environments. These approaches do not allow easy scaling across the wide range of species and environments that are relevant to agriculture, forestry, and horticulture for both commercial and consumer plant care.
  Here we present Bombadil, a foundation model for plant electrophysiology, pretrained without labels on over 4 million hours of electrical signals recorded from 100 plant species in ten distinct environments, including laboratories, greenhouses, commercial orchards, and natural forests. In this way, Bombadil is able to learn the fundamental features of plant electrical signals across a wide array of species and environments. Then, from those same electrical signals, Bombadil tracks changes in seven physiological indicators of plant stress, even among species and stressors with no labels in training.
Signal Processing.comment: 25 pages, 13 figures, 11 tables

Signal Processing.title: From Data to Deployment: A Scoping Review of Empirical Tools, Techniques, and Operational Readiness in Data-Driven 5G/6G Network Optimization
Signal Processing.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to 5G/6G network optimization, yet differences in empirical evidence, evaluation methods, and computational requirements complicate comparisons of reported performance. This scop ing review synthesizes 72 peer-reviewed journal studies pub lished between 2022 and 2026, selected through a PRISMA ScR-informed process from 893 records. The review examines empirical tools, AI/ML techniques, optimization domains, and operational readiness. Evidence classification identifies 37 studies (51.4%) using real-world or physical-testbed evidence only, 25 (34.7%) combining measured and simulated evidence, and 10 (13.9%) relying exclusively on synthetic or simulated data. Offline analysis was the most common evaluation setting, accounting for 45 studies (62.5%). Three principal findings emerge. First, empirical measurements improve contextual relevance, while simulation and digital twins support scalable experimentation but introduce validation challenges. Second, algorithmic effectiveness depends on the optimization objective, data characteristics, and computational constraints rather than model complexity alone. Third, predictive accuracy is more consistently evaluated than the network-level effects of optimization decisions. The review there fore introduces the six-module Evidence Fidelity and Operational Reporting (EFOR) checklist to improve evaluation consistency, reporting transparency, and operational relevance.

Signal Processing.title: ECGWmark: Deep Watermarking for Electrocardiogram Signals
Signal Processing.summary: Wearable electrocardiogram (ECG) recordings pass through multiple networks and systems before automated interpretation, making patient metadata vulnerable to loss. Digital watermarking embeds this metadata directly into the signal. However, conventional ECG watermarking methods fail under temporal desynchronization, and waveform similarity does not guarantee downstream diagnostic preservation. This article presents ECGWmark, a deep watermarking framework for single-lead ECG. A fully convolutional generator embeds the payload without signal quantization, a detector decodes the message frame by frame and verifies watermark presence, and a frozen arrhythmia classifier penalizes changes that would alter diagnostic predictions. To bridge the gap between bit accuracy and whole-message recovery, payloads are protected by extended Hamming codes, validation-selected interleaving, and soft-decision decoding. On the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database, ECGWmark maintains over 90\% bit accuracy under time shifts of 10 to 50 samples, where transform baselines fall to chance level. With the coding layer, the protected 16-bit payload achieves 99.86\% exact recovery on clean segments and sustains over 90\% recovery under time shifts, 10\% sample deletion, and 10\% packet loss. Inter-patient evaluation confirms improved ventricular-beat sensitivity with preserved macro-F1. Requiring only 0.56 million parameters and about 15~ms per segment on a desktop CPU, ECGWmark highlights the need to assess physiological watermarking through whole-message recovery and diagnostic consistency.
Signal Processing.comment: 10 pages, 2 figures, 4 tables

Signal Processing.title: Vision--RF Cooperative ISAC for Dynamic V2I Networks: Adaptive Beam Management and Semantic Clutter Suppression
Signal Processing.summary: We develop a vision--radio-frequency (RF) cooperative integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) framework that jointly uses visual priors and RF observations for transmit-side beam control and receiver-side clutter suppression. Within a narrowband snapshot model, visual target priors and historical RF detections guide control in dynamic vehicle-to-infrastructure networks with roadside clutter. In this framework, posterior angular uncertainty determines beam control and the selection between communication-for-sensing and sensing-for-sensing modes. To reduce sensing overhead while accommodating unreliable visual information, we develop a reliability-adaptive beam scanning scheme that allocates a bounded scan budget according to visual target probabilities and RF history, while reserving an adaptive fraction for exploration. At the receiver, visual geometry identifies clutter support, and RF observations estimate the corresponding complex reflection coefficients. Motion-aware residual filtering is then applied before angle--Doppler detection to suppress clutter while preserving slow-moving targets. Furthermore, communication and sensing power allocation is formulated as a per-direction linear program, subject to signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio constraints evaluated at angles sampled from the posterior distribution and a total-power budget. Simulation results show that the proposed framework improves tracking over static and vision-only beam control and reduces sensing overhead relative to full scanning. The proposed scanning scheme also provides greater robustness to visual blockage than fixed-weight scanning, while the receiver better preserves slow-moving targets than temporal cancellation when visual target information is available.

Signal Processing.title: Does Synchrophasor Attenuation Preclude Detection of High-Frequency Oscillations?
Signal Processing.summary: Recent work suggests that standard synchrophasors are inadequate for capturing high-frequency data center oscillations, primarily due to filtering and windowing attenuation during phasor estimation. We prove that widely used periodogram and RMS energy detectors remain largely robust to it and confirm this by simulation.

Signal Processing.title: Waveguide Deployment Optimization for Pinching-Antenna Systems
Signal Processing.summary: Most existing studies on pinching-antenna systems optimize the antenna positions or activation states under a prescribed waveguide deployment, where mutually parallel waveguides are commonly adopted. However, it remains unclear whether, and under what conditions, such a deployment is optimal from a communication-performance perspective. To fill this gap, this paper investigates long-term waveguide deployment optimization for pinching-antenna systems over a rectangular service region. We first consider the fundamental two-waveguide case and derive a closed-form sufficient condition, jointly determined by the waveguide height and the service-region aspect ratio, under which a deployment parallel to the longer side of the service region is globally optimal. We then consider the general multi-waveguide case, where the orientation and offset of each waveguide are jointly optimized without prescribing any deployment pattern, and develop an adaptive exchange algorithm for the resulting nonconvex optimization problem. We further show that, within the parallel class, the waveguides should be aligned with the longer side of the service region, while in the large-height regime, the globally optimal unrestricted deployment asymptotically concentrates all waveguides on the centerline along the longer side. Numerical results validate the proposed algorithm and reveal how the preferred deployment geometry depends on the waveguide height and service-region shape. In particular, nonparallel deployments can provide noticeable gains in intermediate-height regimes, whereas parallel or center-concentrated deployments become favorable in other regimes.

Signal Processing.title: Signal Design Impacts on GNSS and LEO-PNT L1 Band Acquisition Complexity: A Case Study with Xona Pulsar
Signal Processing.summary:
GNSS signal acquisition is the process of detecting and estimating signal parameters by exploiting correlation operations that provide processing gain and enable the detection of signals below the noise floor. The design of an acquisition engine requires balancing achievable sensitivity, computational complexity, memory requirements, power consumption, and implementation complexity. In particular, increasing coherent and non-coherent integration times improves sensitivity but can significantly increase receiver processing requirements, limiting its applicability in low-power and resource-constrained receivers.
  This paper presents a comparative analysis of L1-band signal acquisition complexity by evaluating the required integration time and corresponding implementation requirements for different signal designs under equivalent acquisition performance targets. The analysis considers the impact of signal characteristics, including spreading codes, secondary codes, modulation, and signal bandwidth, on coherent and non-coherent acquisition performance. For a given attenuation level and target probability of false alarm and detection, the required integration times are derived and translated into acquisition complexity metrics, including arithmetic operations, processing time, and memory requirements.
  The analysis is applied to Pulsar X1, a LEO-enabled PNT signal, and representative GNSS L1 signals to determine under which attenuation, assistance, and integration conditions the higher received power of LEO-PNT translates into reduced receiver acquisition workload. By relating the required integration to arithmetic operations, processing time, and memory requirements, the study provides a receiver-level comparison relevant to both conventional and snapshot-based receivers, where reducing acquisition processing can directly contribute to lower energy consumption.

Signal Processing.title: On the Performance of RIS Transmitter with Receive Combining Techniques
Signal Processing.summary: In this paper, we investigate the impact of practical phase-shift constraint of reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) on multi-antenna systems employing maximal ratio combining (MRC) and receive antenna selection (RAS). Since each element of RIS can apply only a single phase-shift at a given time, the system performance degrades substantially when multiple receive antennas are active simultaneously. To quantify this effect, closed-form outage probability expressions are derived and asymptotic analyses are carried out over Rician fading channels. We show that the practical phase-shift constraint of RIS degrades the diversity order of MRC and in addition, RAS outperforms MRC, contrary to the conventional performance ordering of these techniques.

Signal Processing.title: Joint Subcarrier and Power Allocation for Localization-Oriented Multi-Carrier Underwater ISAC Systems
Signal Processing.summary: Multi-carrier underwater integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) realizes concurrent acoustic communication and localization, yet the frequency selectivity of the acoustic channel creates uneven positioning capabilities across subcarriers. This paper proposes a localization-oriented subcarrier and power allocation scheme for multi-anchor underwater ISAC systems. We build a unified orthogonal subcarrier multiplexing framework and derive closed-form Cramer-Rao bounds (CRBs) under frequency-selective channels with colored noise. We derive a subcarrier-level localization information contribution from the time of arrival Fisher information, which enables localization-oriented resource allocation. We derive several theoretical properties regarding the distance and frequency dependence of the localization information metric, and establish a distance-frequency matching principle. These results provide a theoretical foundation for localization-oriented resource allocation and guide the design of a low-complexity greedy algorithm that improves positioning accuracy. Specifically, the algorithm iteratively allocates subcarriers to minimize the residual positioning-error objective, thereby improving positioning accuracy while satisfying communication quality-of-service (QoS) constraints. Simulations verify that our method yields much lower positioning error bound than uniform, random and high-frequency-first subcarrier allocation in symmetric or asymmetric topologies while guaranteeing communication QoS, achieving superior communication-localization tradeoffs.

Signal Processing.title: How Much AI Is in This Track? Quantifying the Proportion of AI-Generated Stems in Hybrid Music Mixtures
Signal Processing.summary: AI-generated music is increasingly used at the stem level, with producers integrating synthetic drums, basslines, or vocals alongside human-performed instruments. However, current AI music detection systems are binary, treating tracks as either fully AI or fully human. In this paper, we reformulate AI music detection as a regression problem on a continuous AI energy ratio, alpha in [0, 1]. We propose a methodology that leverages a multi-track music dataset to assemble mixtures of human-performed and AI-reconstructed stems (obtained using a neural audio codec) with known proportions of each content type. Using this approach, we first show that a CNN-based model trained on fully AI-generated or human-performed tracks, which achieves >99% accuracy as a binary detector, when faced with mixed content, yields an output that rises with the AI stems' energy contribution, acting as a noisy and miscalibrated estimator. Our analysis of the influence of different stems shows that detection sensitivity depends on the instrument and reflects its frequency content: drums and guitar carry strong codec-artifact signatures, while vocals and bass are less detectable. Based on these insights, we train a similar CNN-based model for regression of alpha, achieving MAE = 0.076 and R^2 = 0.85 on held-out mixtures from the same pipeline. These results suggest that the regression formulation is an initial promising step towards AI-music detection in realistic music production workflows.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted at International Society for Music Information Retrieval Conference (ISMIR 2026)

Signal Processing.title: Physics-Driven Framework for QoS-Constrained Satellite System with Non-Linear PA Distortion
Signal Processing.summary: This work develops a physics-driven self-supervised graph learning framework that directly optimizes the distortion-aware precoder under nonlinear correlated power amplifier (PA) distortion, without relying on expensive optimizer-generated labels for a user-centric satellite system. We minimize nonlinear PA consumption subject to user quality-of-service (QoS) constraints under PA nonlinearity for a downlink multi-input-single-output (MISO) satellite system. Our pipeline jointly designs the precoder and admission control that minimize nonlinear PA consumed power. In particular, a graph neural network (GNN) for the design of a distortion-aware precoder is optimized end-to-end in a self-supervised manner using a differentiable Itô-Hermite model of the true modified Rapp amplifier model. The precoder output by the GNN is used to initialize a low-complexity distortion-aware signal-to-interference-distortion (SINDR) tracking algorithm that jointly optimizes for power and admission control. Our proposed physics-based pipeline closely tracks a successive convex approximation (SCA) based solution in consumed power performance with the advantage of faster runtime and a wide operating range covered during training.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted at IEEE GLOBECOM 2026 Workshops (GC Wkshps)

Signal Processing.title: Holographic Beamforming for Range-Doppler Sidelobe Suppression in OFDM-ISAC
Signal Processing.summary: This paper investigates range--Doppler (RD) sidelobe suppression in an integrated sensing and communications system with a reconfigurable holographic surface (RHS). We jointly design the digital feed precoders and RHS amplitudes to minimize the expected integrated RD sidelobe level over random communication symbols, subject to target-illumination and communication constraints. We then develop an alternating successive convex approximation method that updates the feed and RHS variables through convex quadratic subproblems. Numerical results show that the proposed design consistently reduces normalized RD sidelobe levels across different apertures and configurations, and improves sensing weak-target detectability.

Signal Processing.title: Optical ISAC with Single-Photon Avalanche Diode (SPAD) Arrays
Signal Processing.summary: Single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) arrays offer photon-level sensitivity for sensing in optical integrated sensing and communication (O-ISAC). However, after each detection, a SPAD is blind for a dead time, which saturates the array at high received power. Existing O-ISAC analyses assume linear receivers and do not capture this effect. In this paper, we study ranging with a SPAD array in a monostatic O-ISAC system based on direct-current-biased optical orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (DCO-OFDM). Sampling the array once per dead time, we model the number of pixels that detect a photon in each sampling interval as a binomial random variable whose success probability accounts for the intensity variation of the echo within a dead time. Based on this model, we derive the Cramér-Rao bound (CRB) for range estimation. We show that the SPAD count model of optical wireless communication, which assumes a constant photon rate over a dead time, causes a range bias that depends on the received power. Moreover, unlike for a linear photodiode, saturation degrades the ranging accuracy beyond a sensing-optimal transmit power. The rate-constrained operating point is then the larger of this power and the power needed for the target data rate. Numerical results validate the analysis against a continuous-time photon-counting simulation and show that the proposed model is needed for ranging.
Signal Processing.comment: 5 pages, 4 figures, conference

Signal Processing.title: Joint Deployment and Resource Management for Group-Tag-Based Physical-Layer Authentication and Collaborative Communication in NTN
Signal Processing.summary: Physical-layer authentication (PLA) in non-terrestrial networks (NTNs) has primarily been studied from a security perspective, while its system-level integration with communication remains less explored. We propose the secure adaptive framework for authentication in multi-zone networks (SAFA-MZ), a system-level formulation for the joint management of collaborative group-tag and private-data delivery in NTN, where high-altitude platform station (HAPS) placement, user association, and transmission powers are jointly selected under service and secrecy constraints. Group-level authentication tags and user data are collaboratively transmitted by multiple HAPSs, with artificial noise (AN) mitigating information leakage. We jointly optimize HAPS placement, user association, and power allocation to balance deployment regularity, tag distribution, and user-rate fairness under secrecy, quality-of-service (QoS), power, and coverage constraints. The problem is addressed using a repair-based cross-entropy method (RCEM) and a graph-aware advantage actor-critic (A2C) algorithm (GA2C). Under colluding and non-colluding eavesdropper models, GA2C improves average secrecy spectral efficiency (SSE) by 135--139% over its single-connect baseline and 21.1--23.2% over its baseline without AN. Across ten independent random seeds, GA2C achieves approximately 23.4% and 17.9% higher mean per-user SSE under non-colluding and colluding eavesdropping, respectively, and a 16.2\% higher mean private-rate Jain's index than RCEM. These results quantify the gains of multi-node connectivity and AN within the proposed framework under the evaluated assumptions.
Signal Processing.comment: Substantial revision: the title and author list were updated, RSMA- and differential-privacy-related components were removed, and the manuscript was extensively revised to introduce a joint deployment and resource-management framework for group-tag-based PLA and collaborative communication

Signal Processing.title: Learnable Pilot Design for OFDM-based Deep Joint Source-Channel Coding
Signal Processing.summary: Recent advances in deep joint source-channel coding (DeepJSCC) have shown strong robustness to channel variations in wireless image transmission. However, its integration with orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) typically relies on fixed pilot patterns that are not optimized for receiver- side channel processing. This work introduces Pilot-Efficient DeepJSCC-OFDM (PE-JSCC), which learns pilot placement under a strictly fixed number of pilot symbols via a Gumbel- Top-k-based selector. The learned pilot placement improves end- to-end performance over the conventional Block-JSCC, Comb- JSCC, and Scatter-JSCC baselines. To support high mobility, the receiver incorporates a lightweight axial-attention-based inter- carrier interference (ICI) canceler and a CNN-based channel estimator. Simulation results show that PE-JSCC consistently outperforms fixed pilot patterns across diverse SNRs and remains robust over a wide mobility range.
Signal Processing.comment: Accepted for publication in the 2026 IEEE 103rd Vehicular Technology Conference (VTC2026-Spring)

Signal Processing.title: Timing Skew Estimation of Time-Interleaved ADC based on Inter-Channel Correlations without Computing Derivative of Input Signal
Signal Processing.summary: Time-interleaved analog-to-digital converters (TI-ADCs) enable multi-gigasample-per-second throughput in high-speed applications, but sub-picosecond timing skews among interleaved channels introduce large spectral artifacts that degrade dynamic performance. To continuously track parametric drifts without interrupting normal operation, background calibration is required. However, extracting timing skews under unknown inputs is challenging, and many existing correlation-based methods rely on resource-heavy derivative filters that restrict input bandwidth. This article proposes a novel background timing-skew estimation technique for two-channel TI-ADCs that overcomes these limitations. Closed-form timing-skew expressions are derived using: (a) adjacent-channel cross-correlation combined with single-channel auto-correlation for sinusoidal inputs, and (b) adjacent-channel cross-correlation for Wide-Sense Stationary (WSS) inputs, specifically bandpass-filtered wideband noise and Orthogonal Frequency Division Multiplexed (OFDM) signals. The derived analytical models are validated through comprehensive simulations, offering an efficient framework for real-time background calibration in high-speed data converters.

Signal Processing.title: Beyond the Flat-Spike: Adaptive Sparse CCA for Decaying and Unbalanced Signals
Signal Processing.summary: Sparse Canonical Correlation Analysis (SCCA) is a fundamental statistical tool for identifying linear relationships in high-dimensional, multi-view data.
